articles.title: Aave Risk Adviser Proposes Freezing $1.33 Billion of Core Collateral
articles.excerpt: StakeWise's founder asked for a separate vote on osETH, where $279.4 million of collateral backs loans at about 14 times leverage.
articles.body_md:
Aave's risk adviser LlamaRisk wants to freeze nine more tokens on Aave V3 Core, the lending app's main Ethereum market, in a plan covering $1.33 billion of collateral backing $1.03 billion of loans as of Nov. 9. On Wednesday, one issuer asked for its own vote.

LlamaRisk, which is funded in part by the Aave DAO, posted the [proposal](https://governance.aave.com/t/arfc-repositioning-aave-v3-core-around-established-liquid-collateral/26191) on Aave's governance forum on Nov. 10.

**How a freeze works**

On Aave, users deposit tokens and borrow against them. A freeze blocks new deposits and new borrowing against a token and sets its loan-to-value ratio (the share of a deposit's value a user can borrow) to zero. Existing loans stay open and can be repaid or moved at any time. On frozen reserves still carrying more than $20,000 of debt, the DAO's cut of interest would rise to 99%. LlamaRisk said borrow rates wouldn't change.

**Most of the money sits in ether loops**

Two of the five big tokens are already frozen: Kelp DAO's rsETH since April and Threshold's tBTC since Oct. 31. The new freezes would hit StakeWise's osETH ($279.4 million of collateral backing $256.6 million of debt), Lombard's LBTC ($177.4 million and $72.1 million) and Rocket Pool's rETH ($81.8 million and $35.4 million).

The osETH loans run at about 14 times leverage: deposit staked ether, borrow ether, stake it, repeat.

The debt in scope earns the DAO about $3.7 million a year, LlamaRisk said. If exposure doesn't shrink, the plan allows small, monthly cuts to liquidation thresholds and, as a last step, a WETH borrow-rate rise of up to 1 percentage point. "We will not make abrupt parameter changes that would liquidate significant positions," LlamaRisk wrote.

**StakeWise asks for a separate vote**

A post signed by StakeWise founder Dmitri asked LlamaRisk and the DAO on Nov. 11 to "move the proposed osETH freeze to a separate vote." Lombard and Rocket Pool hadn't posted in the thread by Wednesday evening. No vote had been posted to Snapshot as of Nov. 11, [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/llamarisk-asks-aave-to-freeze-stakewise-lombard-and-rocket-pool-tokens-on-its-v3-core-market/) reported.

*In our opinion: the number to watch is $862 million, the WETH debt tied to the rsETH and osETH loops, because that's where any rate change would land. Aave is asking those borrowers to leave, politely and on their own schedule. The first real test is whether the DAO splits osETH out, as StakeWise asked, before anything reaches a vote.*

articles.title: South Korean Lawmakers Tentatively Back Crypto Tax Delay to 2029
articles.excerpt: The bill hasn't passed. Lawmakers still split over making exchanges hand trading records to the tax office from 2027, two years before any tax is due.
articles.body_md:
South Korea's ruling and main opposition parties tentatively agreed on Wednesday to push the country's crypto income tax back two years, to 2029, [Yonhap reported](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261111011000320). The tax is set to start in January 2027 under current law.

Black Mint [reported Nov. 6](https://blackmint.markets/news/south-korea-crypto-tax-2029/) that the government would seek the delay. This is the first sign the National Assembly will go along.

**No vote yet**

Rep. Oh Gi-hyoung of the ruling Democratic Party, who chairs the tax subcommittee, told reporters the parties found no real differences on the government's two-year plan, per [Yonhap's Korean report](https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20261111170100001). The subcommittee did not pass the bill. Oh said the final vote will come on its last day of review.

Rep. Bae June-young of the opposition People Power Party said the government has to prepare responsibly if it delays again, and that lawmakers would check its progress, Yonhap reported.

The tax was first set for 2022. It was pushed to 2023, then 2025, then 2027, so this would be its fourth delay.

**What the bill changes**

The bill, filed by Democratic Party Rep. Ahn Do-geol from the finance ministry's plan, adds a three-year loss carryforward, [Edaily reported](https://www.edaily.co.kr/News/Read?newsId=03663766645644736). The idea: a losing year could reduce tax owed on gains in the next three years. Today only same-year losses count.

It would also make domestic exchanges send customers' trading records to the National Tax Service from 2027. Crypto moves between exchanges and overseas platforms, so the tax office says it needs the records to work out what each person paid and gained. The agency told Edaily it would use the data only to build a pre-filled filing system before the tax starts, not to tax anyone.

**Two points still open**

Lawmakers still disagree on that 2027 start date for exchange records, and the government opposes raising the tax-free allowance, Yonhap reported. Under current law, individuals would pay 22%, including local tax, on yearly crypto gains above 2.5 million won, [The Korea Herald](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10927485) reported last week.

*In our opinion: a tax first written for 2022 is heading for its fourth delay, and Korea's crypto traders get two more years without it. The detail worth chasing is the records rule, because exchanges could be filing customers' trades with the tax office in 2027, two years before anyone owes a won. The subcommittee's last session settles both questions.*

articles.title: Deutsche Bank Switches On Custody for Bitcoin, Ether and Stablecoins
articles.excerpt: Germany's largest lender now holds private keys for institutional clients in Europe, and it signed a digital-asset deal with its own money manager.
articles.body_md:
Deutsche Bank said on Wednesday that its digital asset custody service is live for paying clients, holding 5 tokens for institutions in Europe, [Reuters reported](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/deutsche-bank-launches-digital-asset-custody-service). It announced the plan in September.

The bank's [product page](https://digitalassets.db.com/) lists them: bitcoin, ether and the USDC, EURC and EURAU stablecoins. It is for institutional investors, companies, governments and wealth managers, not retail customers.

**What custody means here**

Owning crypto comes down to controlling a private key, the secret code that moves coins. A custodian holds those keys for the client. Deutsche Bank says it stores them in hardware security modules (tamper-resistant key vaults), offers warm and cold storage, and lets clients set their own approval steps for transfers. Clients reach it through the bank's Autobahn gateway or its Corporate Bank portal.

The service is booked out of Deutsche Bank AG in Frankfurt and offered across Europe through passporting, and the bank describes it as compliant with the EU's MiCA crypto rules. For now it offers custody, transfers to other parties, and moves between warm and cold storage. "Further capabilities" are planned, the page says.

**A second deal inside the family**

The bank also signed a memorandum of understanding with Deutsche Asset Management, the money manager it mostly owns that was until recently called DWS, Reuters reported. The two will explore commercial and technical work together in digital assets, the bank said, without naming products.

"In the medium term we aim to deliver a fully integrated, regulated ecosystem that supports the custody, tokenisation, and settlement of digital assets," Paul Maley, the bank's global head of trust and securities services, said, per Reuters.

**What the bank didn't say**

It didn't name its first clients, say how many signed up, or publish its fees, [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/deutsche-bank-bitcoin-custody-live) noted. Crypto held this way also isn't covered by a deposit-guarantee scheme, the outlet said, citing the bank's September release.

*In our opinion: Germany's biggest bank opened the vault with a short menu of five tokens. The asset-management deal is the part to follow, because it keeps any new digital product inside one banking group. The bank has also told Reuters it wants to take custody to Asia. The first number worth asking for is the client count, which the bank has kept to itself so far.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Core Details Three Fixed Bugs, One That Could Stall Miners
articles.excerpt: The worst flaw left some mining nodes unable to build blocks after a reorg. Fixes shipped in 30.0 and 29.2 in October 2025; 29.x hit end of life Oct. 27.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin Core published details of three security bugs on Nov. 10, including a High-severity flaw that left some mining nodes unable to build blocks after a reorg. All three were fixed more than a year ago.

Anyone still running an old node is the one with the stake here. The fixes shipped in Bitcoin Core 30.0 on Oct. 10, 2025, and in 29.2 on Oct. 14, 2025, according to the project's [advisories](https://bitcoincore.org/en/security-advisories/). The project waited until the last vulnerable release line, 29.x, reached end of life on Oct. 27, 2026, before publishing the details. None of the three write-ups says whether a bug was ever exploited.

**How a reorg jammed a miner's block template**

A node keeps a mempool, its waiting room for unconfirmed transactions. Version 3 transactions, called TRUC (defined in BIP 431), may have only one unconfirmed parent and one unconfirmed child. Version 28.0 added "sibling eviction," which swaps an existing child for a better-paying one.

During a chain reorganization, when a node drops recent blocks for a competing chain, it puts their transactions back into the mempool. The [High-severity advisory](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/10/disclose-cve-2025-62861/) (CVE-2025-62861) says sibling eviction kept running during that step. That step evicted restored transactions in some cases, leaving the mempool inconsistent, so a miner's block template failed until the node was restarted. Versions 28.0 to 28.2 and 29.0 to 29.1 were affected.

**Two Medium-rated bugs**

The [second flaw](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/10/disclose-cve-2025-62860/) only hit nodes using the optional -whitelist setting, which relaxes limits for trusted peers. Inbound Tor peers show up with the local Tor daemon's address, so whitelisting that range trusted every Tor peer. The advisory says vendor setups led to "thousands of reachable mainnet nodes whitelisting all incoming Tor connections."

The [third](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/10/disclose-cve-2025-62859/) let a malicious peer stall block processing through compact blocks, a bandwidth-saving way to relay new blocks. If the attacker controlled all three of a node's high-bandwidth peers, or the node ran -blocksonly, the stall repeated with no end, the advisory says.

[Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/bitcoin-core-discloses-bugs-that-could-freeze-mining-nodes/) noted these are separate from three bugs the project disclosed on Oct. 28.

*In our opinion: the date to circle is Oct. 27. Once 29.x stopped getting updates, every node still on 28.x or 29.1 and older is running software with publicly documented flaws. Miners and node-in-a-box vendors carry most of that risk, and the fix has been sitting on the download page for 13 months.*

articles.title: Bitmine Reports $6.3 Billion Annual Loss, Nearly All From Ether's Drop
articles.excerpt: Revenue rose to $124.8 million, 97% of it from staking. The 10-K also says Bitmine is still fixing material weaknesses in its internal controls.
articles.body_md:
Bitmine Immersion Technologies lost $6.31 billion in the fiscal year that ended Aug. 31, its annual report filed Tuesday evening shows. Of that, $6.23 billion was an unrealized loss on its ether.

A year earlier, the company had net income of $348.6 million, according to the [10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1829311/000162828026072846/bmnr-20260831.htm). The swing tracks the ether price, not the business.

**Why a falling token shows up as a loss**

Bitmine marks its crypto at fair value, meaning the market price on the reporting date, and books any change straight into profit. "Unrealized" means it didn't sell. If ether falls, the loss appears on the income statement anyway. If it rises, so does reported profit. The filing warns that this will keep causing "significant volatility" in results.

On Aug. 31 the company held 5,901,837 ETH worth $14.56 billion, about 4.9% of circulating supply, plus 211 bitcoin worth $16.6 million.

**Staking now pays most of the bills**

Revenue rose to $124.8 million from $6.1 million. Staking and validation brought in $121.4 million, or 97% of the total. Staking means locking ether to help run the Ethereum network in exchange for rewards, which Bitmine puts at about 2.5% to 4.0% a year, paid in ETH. When ether falls, those rewards are worth less in dollars.

**Follow the money**

Shareholders paid for the stack. Bitmine sold 395.1 million new shares through an at-the-market program, which lets a company sell stock gradually into the market, raising $13.2 billion before costs. It also bought back and retired 20.8 million shares for $353.8 million.

The 10-K also says the company is still working to fix material weaknesses in its internal control over financial reporting.

The buying hasn't stopped. As of Nov. 8, Bitmine held 6,070,092 ETH, or 4.97% of supply, its [Nov. 9 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1829311/000149315226050647/ex99-1.htm) said. Chairman Tom Lee has set 5% as the stopping point. Ether traded near $2,059 at 5:55 a.m. ET Wednesday, down 1.4% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: the loss is on paper, but the shares sold to fund the buying are real, and 395 million of them now split whatever the ether is worth. The release valued the stack at $2,234 per ETH on Nov. 8; Wednesday's price is about 8% lower. The next markers are the 5% line, roughly 40,000 ETH away, and whether the next filing reports those control weaknesses fixed.*

articles.title: FSB Tells Türkiye It Needs a Stablecoin Regime in Crypto Peer Review
articles.excerpt: Türkiye has 7.1 million crypto accounts but no rules written for stablecoins. The FSB's peer review also flags slow bank custody licensing.
articles.body_md:
Türkiye should set up a dedicated rulebook for stablecoins, the Financial Stability Board said Wednesday in a [peer review](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/Peer-Review-of-Turkiye.pdf) of a crypto market that handled nearly $200 billion in transactions in 2025.

The FSB is the Basel-based group that coordinates financial rules for the G20. In 2023 it finished a global framework for crypto and stablecoins, and its members agreed to be checked against it. Türkiye volunteered for this review.

**Where Türkiye stands**

The [review](https://www.fsb.org/2026/11/peer-review-of-turkiye/) says Turkish authorities have made real progress since 2025. Crypto service providers must now register and get licensed by the Capital Markets Board (CMB). Crypto can't be used for domestic payments, and platforms may keep no more than 5% of client crypto in their own wallets. The rest sits with a separate custodian.

The size, per the report:

- more than 7.1 million crypto accounts, though only 51% hold a balance
- about $3 billion of holdings at licensed local providers, per official data cited in the report
- about $0.5 billion in daily crypto trading, against $3.9 billion on Borsa Istanbul

Bitcoin, ether, XRP and USDT make up more than 45% of local holdings.

**The stablecoin gap**

A stablecoin is a token pegged to a currency such as the dollar and backed by reserves. Türkiye treats them like any other crypto asset, the report says, so there are no specific rules on reserves or redemption, the main protections when a coin loses its peg. Some payment-type coins may fall under e-money rules instead.

The report says many users buy dollar stablecoins, mainly USDT, either to hedge against a weaker lira or to move money to foreign platforms. The only lira stablecoin from a local issuer, BiLira, has a market value of about $5.9 million.

The FSB also asks for a financial-stability monitoring framework, tougher supervision and enforcement, and more cross-border information sharing. Bank custody licensing has taken around 12 to 18 months, the report says, and industry firms quoted in it said no licensed bank had yet started offering custody.

*In our opinion: the hole the FSB found is the one that matters most to ordinary users, since a lira holder buying USDT is trusting reserves that no Turkish rule addresses. The report doesn't set a deadline, so the next thing to look for is a draft stablecoin law from Ankara and the first bank actually opening a custody desk.*

articles.title: Kraken's xStocks Adds 200-Plus UK and EU Stock Tokens, Passing 1,500
articles.excerpt: The tokens are backed 1:1 by shares, but holders get no voting rights, and UK and U.S. investors still can't buy them. Hong Kong stocks are next.
articles.body_md:
Payward, the parent of crypto exchange Kraken, put more than 200 tokenized UK and European Union stocks on its xStocks platform Wednesday, taking the lineup past 1,500 assets, the company [announced](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261111700594/en/xStocks-Broadens-Suite-of-Tokenized-Assets-Bringing-Hundreds-of-UK-and-EU-Listed-Equities-Onchain).

British investors are still shut out. The new tokens track UK shares, yet xStocks still can't be sold to investors in the UK, or to U.S. persons, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-11-kraken-parent-payward-adds-200-tokenized-uk-and-european-equities-to-xstocks-offering-437837) from the release.

**How a stock token works**

Each xStock is backed one-for-one: when a token is issued, a real share is bought and held at a regulated custodian for as long as the token trades. The first batch includes LVMH, Rolls-Royce and SAP, [The Defiant reported](https://thedefiant.io/converge/tradfi-and-fintech/xstocks-adds-200-plus-uk-and-eu-stock-tokens-with-gtn). GTN, a brokerage technology firm, handles the buying and custody for the new markets. The tokens then trade on Kraken, on partner venues and on blockchains including Solana, Ethereum and TON.

Legally, it isn't the share. xStocks are tracker certificates issued by Backed Assets (JE) Limited in Jersey, which give price exposure but no shareholder voting rights, the [xStocks legal overview](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/product-legal-overview) says. Kraken's [risk disclosure](https://www.kraken.com/legal/xstocks) adds that holders have no claim on the company's assets in a liquidation and pay fees set out in the prospectus, so returns won't match owning the stock.

**The size so far**

- more than $1.1 billion in assets under management
- more than $45 billion in total trading volume
- more than 550,000 holders
- available in more than 110 markets

Those holder numbers compare with more than 200,000 in September, The Block reported. Payward says hundreds of Hong Kong-listed stocks will follow within weeks. The London Stock Exchange, which partnered with Payward in September, plans to list xStocks on its LSE 24 venue in 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

This is not financial advice.

*In our opinion: Rolls-Royce now comes as a token in more than 110 markets, just not in the UK, where it's based. Holder numbers more than doubled since September, so the platform is growing, but on $1.1 billion it's still small next to the markets it tracks. The clock to watch is the LSE 24 approval, the point where a British exchange itself starts listing the tokens.*

articles.title: Fed's Paulson Says 'Further Gradual Tightening Seems Appropriate'
articles.excerpt: Paulson listed three things that would make her move faster and said she isn't seeing them yet. Goolsbee called October CPI "borderline disturbing."
articles.body_md:
Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said Tuesday evening, Nov. 10, that "further gradual tightening seems appropriate," in [prepared remarks](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/the-economy/monetary-policy/261110-81st-annual-field-meeting-capstone-speech) delivered the same day consumer prices were reported up 0.4% for October.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee told [PBS NewsHour](https://www.pbs.org/video/rising-prices-1794349770/) that report was "borderline disturbing." The Fed's next decision is due at its [Dec. 8-9 meeting](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm).

For crypto holders, the stake is the price of money. Higher policy rates lift what cash and Treasuries pay, which raises the bar for assets that pay no interest, such as bitcoin.

**Paulson named three triggers for moving faster**

Paulson said she backed the Fed's September increase and its October hold. "Skipping a meeting is a matter of pace, not direction," she said. She prefers small steps so families, businesses and community banks can adjust to higher borrowing costs.

She would act more quickly if inflation expectations drift up, wage pressures build or underlying inflation moves higher. "Right now, that's not what I'm seeing," she said, adding that long-term expectations are well anchored.

**Goolsbee pointed to services and the AI build-out**

Goolsbee said the most troubling part of the report was services inflation, which he said is "not coming down" and is probably not mostly driven by oil or tariffs. He also tied some cost pressure to demand from the data-center build-out for AI. Asked by PBS host Geoff Bennett about Governor Christopher Waller's openness to a half-point December increase, he didn't commit. "Everything is always on the table," he said.

How the tool works: the Fed sets a target for the federal funds rate, what banks charge each other for overnight loans. Raising it pushes up borrowing costs across the economy, which is meant to slow spending and, in time, prices. Services prices get close attention because they follow wages and local demand more than one-off shocks such as an oil spike.

Bitcoin was near $73,680 at 11:54 p.m. ET Tuesday, down 1.3% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: the argument inside the Fed has moved from whether to raise rates to how fast. Paulson listed exactly what would make her hurry, and she said she isn't seeing any of it yet. That makes wage data and inflation-expectation surveys the numbers to check before Dec. 9, when the decision lands.*

articles.title: Tron Inc. Profit Rises 22% to $14.9 Million as Per-Share Earnings Fall
articles.excerpt: Earnings per share fell to 3 cents from 11 cents as the share count more than quadrupled. The toy business lost money; the profit came from TRX gains and staking.
articles.body_md:
Tron Inc., a Nasdaq-listed toy maker that now holds most of its value in TRX tokens, said Tuesday its third-quarter net income rose 22% to $14.9 million. Basic earnings per share fell to 3 cents from 11 cents.

The gap comes from share count. The company averaged 474.4 million basic shares in the quarter, up from 110 million a year earlier, its [quarterly filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1956744/000149315226050474/form10-q.htm) shows. Profit grew, but it was split among more than four times as many shares. On a diluted basis, which counts shares that could still be issued, EPS slipped to 3 cents from 4 cents.

**Where the profit came from**

None of it came from toys. The theme-park merchandise business grew sales to $1.19 million from $1.10 million but still lost $573,354 at the operating level. The profit came from:

- $16.3 million of unrealized gains on its tokens
- $3.18 million of unrealized staking income, up 41%
- a $106,228 realized loss on converting TRX

"Unrealized" means paper gains that rise or fall with the TRX price.

How the staking works: the company deposits TRX with JustLend, a lending app on the Tron network, and gets sTRX back. Each sTRX becomes worth more TRX over time as voting rewards and fees from renting out network "energy" build up. That rising exchange rate is what the company books as staking income.

**Who owns it**

The tokens were worth $257.8 million on Sept. 30, out of $275.2 million in total assets. Bravemorning Ltd., owned by director Weike Sun, held about 88.5% of the voting power, the filing says. The filing names Sun as the father of Tron founder Justin Sun and flags possible conflicts of interest, including with JustLend and the firm that set up the company's wallet.

The company also signed an at-the-market deal on Oct. 14 to sell up to $200 million of new stock. It had sold none by the filing date. On Oct. 18 it was elected one of the Tron network's 27 "Super Representatives," the validators that produce blocks, which pays rewards in TRX.

*In our opinion: this is a token treasury that happens to sell souvenirs, and the 10-Q says so in plain numbers. The figure to follow is the share count, because that $200 million stock program, if used, would split future profits further. The next filing will show whether any of it was tapped.*

articles.title: Goldman, Citi Among Banks Backing $270 Million Stablecoin, Report Says
articles.excerpt: The money covers five years of running costs for a planned U.S. issuer codenamed Project Faro. It has no chief executive yet and aims to launch in early 2027.
articles.body_md:
Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank are among the banks that have committed about $270 million to a joint stablecoin company, [Bloomberg](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/banking-law/goldman-citi-among-banks-in-270-million-stablecoin-backing) reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The money is meant to pay for five years of operations at the planned issuer, codenamed Project Faro, which is expected to be incorporated in the U.S., according to the report. None of the banks or the venture has commented publicly on it, [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/goldman-citi-and-other-banks-reportedly-fund-270-million-stablecoin-initiative/) reported.

**Two issuers hold most of the market**

The bank group is going after a market that two companies dominate. Stablecoins in circulation totaled about $292.8 billion on Tuesday evening, with Tether's USDT at about $175.8 billion and Circle's USDC at about $70.0 billion, per [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins).

**How a stablecoin issuer makes money**

A stablecoin is a token meant to stay worth $1. Buyers hand over dollars, and the issuer holds those dollars in reserve, mostly as cash and short-term government debt, so it can pay anyone back on request. The issuer keeps the interest the reserves earn. Project Faro's $270 million is a different pot: it pays for running the company, while the reserves would come from the people who buy the token.

**Twenty-one firms, no CEO yet**

The 21 firms said on Sept. 1 that they would form the company in the second half of 2026, subject to closing conditions. A dollar token comes first, with a euro version the next priority among other Group of Seven currencies, and the group is aiming for a commercial launch in the first half of 2027, [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/goldman-citi-join-global-banks-in-270-million-stablecoin-venture--bloomberg-5016335) reported. Members also include Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Fidelity Investments and MUFG Bank.

The venture still has no name. It also has no chief executive; backers are still searching for one, per the report.

The reports don't say how much each bank is putting in, whether the money is equity, or which blockchain the token will use. The group has said it plans to follow the U.S. GENIUS Act and the EU's MiCA rules where they apply.

*In our opinion: the stake is the interest on reserves, which today goes mostly to Tether and Circle on about $246 billion of combined tokens. A bank-owned issuer would compete for that income with five years of running costs already paid for. The next checkable steps are a company name, a CEO hire and a chosen blockchain, and none of them exists yet.*

articles.title: SEC Filed 348 Enforcement Cases in Fiscal 2026, Down From 456
articles.excerpt: Money orders totaled $1.095 billion, the lowest since 2008 by a Reuters count. The SEC also set up a data office whose work includes tracing blockchain flows.
articles.body_md:
The Securities and Exchange Commission brought 348 enforcement actions in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30, the agency [said Tuesday](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026-113-sec-announces-enforcement-annual-results-fiscal-year-2026), down from 456 the year before.

Money orders totaled $1.095 billion. That is the lowest level since 2008, according to a [Reuters review](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-10/us-sec-enforcement-activity-plummets-in-2026-with-fewer-fines-and-cases) of agency figures, which also put the median at 715 cases a year from 2005 to 2025.

**Where the $1.095 billion came from**

- Disgorgement and interest: $752 million
- Civil penalties: $343 million
- Returned to investors: about $731 million, to more than 250,000 people

A court in a separate, non-SEC case deemed $235 million of that disgorgement already satisfied, the release says.

How the categories work: disgorgement makes a defendant give back profits from the violation, while a civil penalty is a fine on top. Of the 348 actions, 235 were standalone cases. The other 113 were "follow-on" proceedings that bar people from parts of the industry after a criminal conviction or court order.

Two-thirds of standalone cases charged at least one individual. The agency also suspended trading 13 times over suspected manipulation of Asia-based companies' shares.

**A new office that reads blockchains**

The enforcement division launched an Office of Super Intelligence and Analytics, whose work includes "improved blockchain and financial-flow analysis," the release says. The SEC also signed an agreement with the CFTC on joint enforcement over products that span securities and derivatives. The release doesn't say how many fiscal 2026 cases involved crypto.

Chairman Paul Atkins said case counts and dollar totals "are not the only or most telling measures" of the program. Enforcement Director David Woodcock said the division had reviewed its docket and focused on "consequential misconduct."

*In our opinion: the case count fell about 24% in a year, and the agency's leaders say counts and dollar totals aren't the best yardstick. For crypto, the item to follow is the new analytics office and its blockchain tracing. Fiscal 2027's first filings will show what that work turns up.*

articles.title: U.S. Prices Rise 0.4% in October, Beating Forecasts Before Fed Meeting
articles.excerpt: Core prices rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast. Traders now fully price a December hike and put half-point odds at 13.6%, CME FedWatch shows.
articles.body_md:
U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than the 0.3% economists expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. ET. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9.

Core CPI, which leaves out food and energy, rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/cpi-inflation-report-october-2026.html) reported, citing a Dow Jones survey. Headline prices had climbed 0.6% in September.

**Why one monthly number moved bonds**

The consumer price index tracks what a fixed basket of goods and services costs from month to month. Economists watch the core reading more closely because gasoline and groceries swing hard. A 0.3% monthly pace, kept up for a year, works out to roughly 3.6%. The Fed targets 2%.

There is no annual figure this time. The government shutdown in October 2025 stopped the bureau from collecting enough data, so it had nothing to compare against, [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2026/11/10/consumer-price-index-october-2026-federal-reserve/4541794322678/) and CNBC reported.

**Food and shelter did the lifting**

- Food rose 0.5%, with beef up 0.9%.
- Energy rose 0.7% and gasoline 1%, after gasoline's 9.1% jump in September.
- Shelter rose 0.3% and made up more than 30% of the increase, the bureau said.
- Used cars and trucks fell 1.2%.

**Fed officials spoke on both sides of the release**

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in London before the data that a hot reading would put a half-point hike in play. "Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk," he said, as [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/us-bonds-treasurys-yields.html) reported. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said after the release that she sees a need for two more quarter-point increases.

Traders now fully price a quarter-point hike in December and put the odds of a half point at 13.6%, up from about zero before the report, per CME Group's FedWatch tool. The 10-year Treasury yield rose more than 14 basis points to 5.004%. The Fed's range sits at 3.75%-4%.

Bitcoin fell 2.8% over 24 hours to about $72,900 at 12:05 p.m. ET, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: the shutdown took away the yearly number, but the monthly one did the talking anyway. Core has now printed 0.3% three months running, CNBC's breakdown shows, and Logan wants two more hikes. The next test is producer prices on Friday, then the PCE report later this month.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Hits Lowest Since Aug. 20 as ETFs Shed $1 Billion in 3 Days
articles.excerpt: Spot bitcoin ETFs lost $201 million on Monday, Farside data show. Ether fell harder, down 5.1% to about $2,021 after the hot October CPI report.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell to about $72,900 by midday Tuesday, its lowest price since Aug. 20 in CoinGecko's hourly data, as hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data added to three straight days of fund outflows.

The coin was down 2.8% over 24 hours at 12:05 p.m. ET, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). It had traded as high as about $75,300 on Monday evening.

**Three days, about $1.04 billion out**

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs have lost money on each of the last three trading days, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show:

- Nov. 5: $430.2 million out
- Nov. 6: $411.9 million out
- Nov. 9: $201.0 million out

BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $213.2 million of Monday's exits, while Bitwise's BITB took in $22.1 million. Tuesday's figures aren't out yet.

**How ETF flows reach the price**

A spot ETF holds actual bitcoin. When investors sell more shares than they buy, authorized participants (the large trading firms that create and redeem shares) hand shares back, and the issuer sells or delivers the matching coins. Days of outflows mean bitcoin leaving the funds.

Tuesday's push came from the October consumer price index, which rose 0.4% against a 0.3% forecast. Traders now fully price a quarter-point Fed rate hike on Dec. 9, per CME Group's FedWatch tool as cited by [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/cpi-inflation-report-october-2026.html). Higher rates raise the return on cash and bonds, which competes with assets that pay no interest, like bitcoin.

Ether fell further, down 5.1% to about $2,021 over the same 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum). The Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 32, in its "fear" band.

*In our opinion: the outflows started before Tuesday's inflation data, so the CPI report landed on a market that was already shrinking its ETF bets. The tally worth checking is Tuesday's Farside number tonight, which will show whether the run reaches a fourth day.*

articles.title: FinCEN's MEXC Cutoff Takes Effect Dec. 10, With No End Date Set
articles.excerpt: The Federal Register notice names MEXC units in the Seychelles, Estonia, Switzerland and the UK, and lets FinCEN grant exemptions later.
articles.body_md:
FinCEN's order cutting MEXC Global off from U.S. financial institutions takes effect Dec. 10, 2026, and has no end date, according to the notice published in the [Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22962/imposition-of-special-measure-prohibiting-the-transmittal-of-funds-involving-mexc-global) on Tuesday.

[Black Mint reported Nov. 6](https://blackmint.markets/news/fincen-cuts-off-mexc-global/) that the Treasury bureau had issued the order. Publication starts the 30-day clock.

**What banks and payment firms have to stop**

From Dec. 10, any covered U.S. financial institution is barred from sending funds to or receiving funds from MEXC Global. The order defines a "transmittal of funds" to include crypto as well as dollars. FinCEN kept the power to attach conditions to transfers or grant exemptions later.

The ban reaches beyond one company name. The notice lists MEXC Global Ltd in the Seychelles, MEXC Estonia, GIDA Technology AG in Switzerland and MXC Global Ltd in the UK, plus two former Singapore entities and any successors.

**What FinCEN alleges**

FinCEN alleges MEXC sent or received nearly $1.5 billion in direct and indirect exposure to transactions tied to Russian sanctions evasion, including $232 million in direct transactions with entities sanctioned by the U.S., EU or UK. The order names Garantex and its successor Grinex among them. These are FinCEN's findings, not a court ruling.

MEXC said on Nov. 7 that it was reviewing the order with its legal and compliance teams and intends "to engage constructively with FinCEN." The exchange said it was "operating normally" and had begun an independent review of its anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls, in a [statement](https://www.mexc.com/announcements/article/statement-regarding-fincen-s-november-6-order-17827791539626) on its site.

The order rests on section 9714 of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act, which lets Treasury block transfers involving a foreign firm it finds to be of "primary money laundering concern" tied to Russian illicit finance. It is separate from an OFAC sanctions listing.

The published order grants no exemptions yet. It says FinCEN may add them later.

articles.title: MARA Sells 13,597 Bitcoin for $1.1 Billion and Plans to Keep Selling
articles.excerpt: The miner used $750 million to clear its bitcoin-backed loans. Less than 5% of its remaining coins are now lent out or pledged, down from about 57% in September.
articles.body_md:
MARA Holdings sold 13,597 bitcoin for about $1.1 billion after Sept. 30, at an average near $81,039 a coin, its [third-quarter shareholder letter](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507605/000150760526000026/q326shareholderletter.htm) filed Monday shows. It expects to sell more.

That is about 40% of the 34,012 bitcoin the miner held at the end of September. It is also roughly six times the 2,247 coins its machines mined in the whole quarter, per the company's [earnings call](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/10/mara-holdings-mara-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

**Most of the cash went to lenders**

MARA used $750 million to fully repay its bitcoin-backed term loans, which returned 17,477 coins it had pledged as collateral. Less than 5% of its remaining bitcoin is now lent out or pledged, [CoinDesk reported](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/10/bitcoin-miner-mara-sold-13-597-btc-for-usd1-1-billion-in-six-weeks-plans-to-sell-more) from the letter, down from about 57% at quarter-end.

How that loan worked: in August MARA borrowed against its coins while bitcoin traded around $64,000, to help pay for Long Ridge, a natural-gas power plant it is buying. Selling near $81,000 to repay it left what the company calls an estimated net benefit of $170 million. The letter doesn't give the dates or venues of the sales.

**A miner that used to hold every coin**

MARA began allowing sales of newly mined bitcoin in 2025 and this year widened that to coins on its balance sheet. It sold about 26,984 bitcoin for $1.9 billion in the first nine months of 2026. "We expect to continue to monetize bitcoin," the letter says, naming liquidity and capital projects. The company has also authorized buybacks of up to $500 million, [BeInCrypto](https://beincrypto.com/mara-sells-13597-bitcoin-after-q3/) and the call transcript show.

Mining itself earned less. Third-quarter revenue fell 35% to $164.2 million. Net income of $632.1 million rested on an $885.3 million unrealized gain on its bitcoin.

Bitcoin was near $74,160 at 5:59 a.m. ET Tuesday, up 0.1% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: coins sold at an average $81,039 would fetch about $74,160 today, so the timing helped MARA's books. The bigger shift is the job description. A company that once kept every coin it mined is now using them like a credit line for power plants and data centers, and the next number to check is what's left on the balance sheet in the fourth-quarter letter.*

articles.title: Coinbase, Kalshi and Four Firms Back CFTC Over Single-Stock Perps
articles.excerpt: The trade group suing the CFTC files its reply Tuesday. A judge already found the group likely to win on the law but denied an emergency order on Nov. 3.
articles.body_md:
Six trading firms led by Coinbase and Kalshi asked a federal judge on Monday, Nov. 9, to let perpetual futures on individual U.S. stocks keep trading, in a [letter motion and proposed amicus brief](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/75062269/capital-markets-alliance-association-v-commodity-futures-trading/) filed in Manhattan. The other side's reply is due Tuesday.

Kraken parent Payward, trading firms DRW and Jump Trading, and a crypto venture investor signed on too; the full list is in the filing. An amicus, or friend-of-the-court, brief lets outsiders argue a case they aren't party to.

**How a perp differs from a future**

A normal future expires on a set date, when the trade settles. A perpetual never expires. Instead, traders on one side pay the other a regular "funding" fee that keeps the contract's price close to the stock's. Under federal law, security futures are overseen jointly by the CFTC and the SEC, while security-based swaps belong to the SEC alone.

**The two arguments**

The Capital Markets Alliance Association, whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-10-coinbase-kalshi-payward-back-cftc-perps-436971), sued the CFTC on Nov. 3. It says the contracts are security-based swaps and that the agency had no power to approve them. Applications from Kalshi, Coinbase Derivatives and Bitnomial were deemed approved on Nov. 2 after a 45-day review window passed without objection. Alliance secretary Adam Ford said the rollout "erodes investor protection," per [Unchained via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/coinbase-kalshi-jump-trading-urge-094511851.html).

The six firms argue the law asks only for delivery at some point in the future, not on a fixed date. A ruling for the alliance would "send equity perpetuals back offshore," their brief says, because the SEC has no framework for retail trading of listed security-based swaps.

**Where the case stands**

On Nov. 3, Judge Valerie Caproni denied the alliance's request for a temporary restraining order, finding it hadn't shown irreparable harm. Her order also found the group probably would win its claim that the CFTC exceeded its authority. The case is assigned to Judge Lorna Schofield, and the bid for a preliminary injunction is still pending. Black Mint [reported the lawsuit](https://blackmint.markets/news/cboe-citadel-sue-cftc-stock-perps/) on Nov. 3.

*In our opinion: the line in that TRO order is the one to read twice. The products survived round one because the harm looked too far off, and the judge sided with the alliance on the law. Tuesday's reply and Judge Schofield's injunction ruling decide whether U.S. stock perps stay onshore.*

articles.title: Brent Falls Below $90 for the First Time Since August on Iran Remarks
articles.excerpt: Brent is about 22% below its Oct. 30 high of $118. Oil feeds inflation, and U.S. consumer price data lands at 8:30 a.m. ET today.
articles.body_md:
Brent crude fell below $90 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since August, after President Donald Trump said further U.S. strikes on Iran were not needed for now. The global benchmark was down 2.65% at $90.14 at 5:33 a.m. ET, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/oil-prices-trump-iran.html), after January contracts dipped under $90 earlier.

The [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/07bdb58c-4557-4def-b8cb-db9be304fd72) put the day's low at $89.21, down as much as 3.6%. U.S. WTI crude was near $84.78, down 2.4%, per CNBC.

**Two days, two drops**

Brent settled down 5.85% on Monday, [Reuters reported](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/commodities/oil-prices-fall-as-trump-signals-pause-in-military-action-against-iran-126111000067_1.html), and it is now about 22% below the six-month high of $118 it reached on Oct. 30. Trump said on Monday he would hold off on new strikes after appeals from countries in the region, including Qatar's prime minister, while keeping a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now. Reuters also said attacks on shipping in the strait are still taking place.

Not everyone expects a quick slide. "Prices are unlikely to fall below $90 per barrel for Brent without more durable signs of de-escalation and a US-Iran deal," Gregory Brew of Eurasia Group said in a note cited by Reuters.

**Why oil reaches crypto**

Fuel costs feed straight into consumer prices. When oil climbs, inflation tends to run hotter, which pushes rate expectations up and makes assets that pay no interest, like bitcoin, less attractive to hold. Cheaper oil works the other way. That link matters today because October U.S. inflation data comes out at 8:30 a.m. ET.

Bitcoin was near $74,160 at 5:59 a.m. ET, up 0.1% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

articles.title: Ether ETFs Lose $184.6 Million, the Most in a Day Since Oct. 6
articles.excerpt: BlackRock's ETHA made up $119.3 million of Monday's exit. Ether funds are down $549.8 million in November, with one inflow day in six.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot ether ETFs had a net outflow of $184.6 million on Monday, Nov. 9, their biggest one-day exit since Oct. 6, when $201.9 million left, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/ethereum-etf-flow-all-data/) data show.

That leaves the funds down a net $549.8 million across November's first six trading sessions. Only one of those days, Nov. 4, brought money in ($53.0 million). In October the ether funds lost $1.61 billion in all.

**BlackRock's ETHA took most of the hit**

BlackRock's iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) accounted for $119.3 million of Monday's outflow. Grayscale's Ethereum Mini Trust, which trades under the ticker ETH, lost $25.0 million, and Fidelity's FETH lost $19.1 million. One small fund took in $1.6 million.

Bitcoin funds were no different. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $201.0 million on Monday, their third straight day of outflows, as BlackRock's IBIT shed $213.2 million, per [Farside's bitcoin table](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/). November's bitcoin ETF total stands at minus $1.48 billion over six sessions.

**What a flow number measures**

A flow figure counts shares created or redeemed, not price moves. When investors sell more ETF shares than others want to buy, large trading firms called authorized participants hand shares back to the fund. The fund then pays them out in cash or in the coins themselves, so its ether holdings shrink. An outflow day means less ether sat inside these funds at the close.

Prices moved less than 1% overnight. Ether was near $2,121 at midnight ET Tuesday, down 0.6% over 24 hours, and bitcoin was near $74,750, up 0.2%, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum).

The next test lands at 8:30 a.m. ET Tuesday, when the Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes October's consumer price index, on its [release schedule](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm).

*In our opinion: five outflow days out of six is a ratio no fund issuer puts in a brochure. For scale, October's $1.61 billion exit took a full month, and November is already about a third of the way there with three weeks left. The flow figures for Tuesday, inflation day, are the next ones worth checking.*

articles.title: Elliptic Says Binance Hack Funds Went Through Six Homemade Tokens
articles.excerpt: About 117,000 stolen NEAR, roughly $430,000, passed through tokens that cost about $90 each to make. Nobody outside the network traded them, Elliptic says.
articles.body_md:
Launderers moving money from the Binance hack created at least six meme tokens on the NEAR blockchain and pushed about 117,000 stolen NEAR, roughly $430,000, through them between Nov. 5 and 7, blockchain analytics firm [Elliptic said Monday](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/north-korea-meme-coins-binance-hack/).

Elliptic values the Oct. 29 theft at $6.4 billion. The [FBI said Oct. 31](https://www.fbi.gov/investigate/cyber/alerts/2026/north-korea-responsible-for-6-billion-binance-attack) that North Korea was responsible, a finding North Korea rejected, Black Mint [reported Nov. 2](https://blackmint.markets/news/north-korea-denies-fbi-binance-hack/).

**How the token trick works**

A liquidity pool is a pot of two tokens on a decentralized exchange that anyone can swap against. Elliptic said the launderers made a new token, paired it with NEAR in its own pool, and bought the token with stolen NEAR from one set of wallets. A second set of wallets then sold the token back into the same pool and took out NEAR. The stolen funds never moved straight from one wallet to the other, so the sellers looked like traders who had made a profit.

Each token cost about 25 NEAR (around $90) to create, Elliptic said. The tokens carried cartoon-style logos, including one with Elon Musk's image, and Elliptic said there is no suggestion he has any connection to them.

**Nobody else was buying**

Wallets in the laundering network made every sale of all six tokens, according to the report. Outside buyers showed up only in a few small purchases of one token, under 1% of its volume. Five of the six token creators were paid from a wallet selling the previous token, 2 to 13 minutes before each launch. None of the six has traded since Nov. 8.

Elliptic said the launderers used the same idea on Tron on Nov. 2 and a related route on Solana on Nov. 3. It first saw the method in the 2025 Bybit case, where at least $24 million moved this way.

The token-launch tool, exchange and wallet app involved "did nothing wrong," Elliptic said.

Elliptic told compliance teams not to treat funds arriving from a liquidity pool as clean by default, especially when newly created tokens are involved. About 11.8 million NEAR ($43.7 million) from the Binance theft has not moved yet.

articles.title: Bank of Japan Members Split on How Fast to Lift Rates From 1.25%
articles.excerpt: One opinion puts Japan's neutral rate considerably above 1%. Another warns the next hike could weigh on the economy. The next meeting is Dec. 17-18.
articles.body_md:
Bank of Japan policymakers disagreed over how quickly to raise the 1.25% policy rate, a [summary of opinions](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/opinion_2026/opi261030.pdf) from the Oct. 29-30 meeting shows. It came out at 8:50 a.m. Tokyo time Tuesday, or 6:50 p.m. ET Monday.

The board held the rate at that October meeting in an 8-1 vote. Member Hajime Takata dissented and proposed 1.5%, the [policy statement](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k261030a.pdf) shows.

**Some want to reach "neutral" soon**

The neutral rate is the level that neither speeds up nor slows down an economy. One opinion said the bank needs "to step up the pace" of getting there. Another said it must reach neutral "soon," and a third called for doing so "at an early stage." One opinion put Japan's neutral rate "considerably above 1 percent."

**Others want to wait**

Two opinions backed holding in October to study risks and "the cumulative effects of past rate hikes." Another warned that a future hike could "weigh on the economy and push down underlying CPI inflation."

How the document works: each board member and government representative writes up their own remarks under a word limit, and Governor Kazuo Ueda edits them. No names are attached, so the summary doesn't show how many members hold each view, as [EconoTimes noted](https://econotimes.com/BOJ-Opinions-Show-Split-Over-Pace-of-Further-Rate-Increases-1774140).

On prices, one opinion projected that consumer prices excluding fresh food will rise more than 3% from a year earlier toward the end of the fiscal year. Four opinions touched on wages, and one said the outcome of next spring's wage negotiations "warrants attention."

A higher BOJ rate also makes it more expensive to borrow in yen, including for investors outside Japan. Bitcoin was near $74,750 at midnight ET Tuesday, up 0.2% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

The next policy meeting is Dec. 17-18, on the BOJ's [meeting calendar](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm).

*In our opinion: the board's argument has moved from whether to raise rates to how fast, and October already had one vote for 1.5%. Full minutes of the October meeting arrive Dec. 23, after the December decision. Until then, the wage data is what one member said "warrants attention."*

articles.title: Securitize Agrees to Buy River One as Q3 Revenue Rises 13%
articles.excerpt: The tokenization firm also posted a $66.3 million net loss, about $60 million of it from listing-related charges, and approved a $50 million buyback.
articles.body_md:
Securitize, the company that puts funds and stocks on blockchains for managers like BlackRock and ARK Invest, agreed Monday to buy lender River One and reported third-quarter revenue of $18.6 million, up 13% from a year earlier. Its shares rose about 10% after hours, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/tokenization-platform-securitize-reports-gains-expands-into-asset-backed-finance.html).

The deal moves Securitize from issuing tokens to lending against assets. River One, founded in New York in 2025, does warehouse financing: short-term credit that lenders use to fund new loans, backed by pools of small-business loans, receivables and similar assets, [Securitize said](https://investors.securitize.io/news/news-details/2026/Securitize-to-Acquire-River-One-Connecting-Stablecoin-Capital-to-the-6-Trillion-Asset-Backed-Finance-Market/default.aspx). Terms weren't disclosed. The company expects the deal to close in the fourth quarter.

**Two ways the business gets paid**

Tokenizing a fund means issuing a blockchain token that stands for a share in it, so it can move and settle around the clock. Securitize charges for that work, and it also earns by running fund back offices. Per its [results release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-302933834.html), tokenization revenue rose 28% to $11.5 million while asset-servicing revenue fell 6% to $7.2 million.

Tokenized assets on the platform stood at $4.8 billion on Sept. 30, up 9%. The quarterly average was a company-record $5.0 billion.

**The loss behind the growth**

Net loss was $66.3 million, or 41 cents a share, after a $4.1 million profit a year earlier. The company said about $60 million of the loss came from largely non-cash charges tied to its July listing on the NYSE through a merger with Cantor Equity Partners II. Operating costs rose 183% to $42.2 million. Adjusted EBITDA, which leaves those charges out, was a $2.0 million loss.

The board approved buybacks of up to $50 million through Dec. 31, 2027. Securitize ended September with about $298.9 million in cash and no debt. Its release lists the risk that the River One deal doesn't close on the expected terms or timeline, or at all.

*In our opinion: the line to follow is asset servicing, the only revenue stream that shrank, as assets under administration fell 29% to $25.2 billion. Securitize is leaning on token fees to carry growth while it adds a lending arm on top. The fourth-quarter closing date for River One is the first checkpoint.*

articles.title: Schwab Crypto Adds Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink Trading
articles.excerpt: The brokerage's crypto menu grows from two tokens to five. Every trade costs 0.75% of its dollar value, and accounts aren't offered in New York or Louisiana.
articles.body_md:
Charles Schwab clients can now buy and sell solana, avalanche and chainlink, the brokerage [said Monday](https://pressroom.aboutschwab.com/press-releases/press-release/2026/Charles-Schwab-Makes-Solana-Avalanche-and-Chainlink-Available-to-Trade-Through-Schwab-Crypto-Accounts/default.aspx), taking its Schwab Crypto service from two tokens to five.

Until now, Schwab's direct crypto offer was bitcoin and ether. The three new listings are its first beyond those two.

**What clients pay**

Schwab charges 75 basis points, or 0.75%, on the dollar value of each trade. On a $1,000 purchase, that's $7.50. The coins sit in the same view as stocks and funds on Schwab.com, the Schwab Mobile app and thinkorswim, the company's trading platform.

Per the release's disclosures, the accounts are run by Charles Schwab Premier Bank, and the crypto in them isn't FDIC-insured or SIPC-protected (the two programs that cover bank deposits and brokerage accounts). Schwab Crypto isn't available in New York, Louisiana or U.S. territories.

**Three different jobs**

The new tokens do different things. Solana and Avalanche are blockchains that run apps and payments, and SOL and AVAX pay their fees. Chainlink is an oracle network, a service that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain apps; LINK pays its node operators.

At 5:55 p.m. ET, solana traded near $86.89, avalanche near $8.64 and chainlink near $10.69, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/solana).

**A slow, staged rollout**

Schwab Crypto opened to early-access clients in May and to all eligible retail clients in October. The company first said in late August it would add these three tokens, [Unchained reported](https://unchainedcrypto.com/schwab-opens-solana-avalanche-and-chainlink-trading-to-its-retail-crypto-clients/), without a date.

"We continue to expand Schwab Crypto to give clients greater choice and flexibility," said Joe Vietri, Schwab's head of digital assets. The release said more assets will come over time but didn't name any.

*In our opinion: Schwab adds coins the way it adds anything, carefully and with a long disclosure page attached. About 11 weeks passed between the August plan and Monday's listings. The number to keep an eye on is that 0.75% fee, because it's what clients pay on every trade and what Schwab earns, and the next listing announcement will show whether the menu keeps growing.*

articles.title: October CPI Will Skip the Annual Inflation Rate, BLS Says
articles.excerpt: The 12-month rate was 3.7% in September. Tuesday's report will show only monthly changes, because October 2025 prices were never collected.
articles.body_md:
Tuesday's consumer price report will arrive without its best-known number. The Bureau of Labor Statistics won't publish 12-month changes for most October CPI series, including headline and core, when the report comes out at 8:30 a.m. ET, [the agency says](https://www.bls.gov/cpi/additional-resources/2025-federal-government-shutdown-impact-cpi-faq.htm).

That annual rate is the figure most people mean by inflation. In September it was 3.7%, up from 3.4% in August, with core prices (everything but food and energy) up 2.6%, per the [September CPI release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.nr0.htm).

**Why the number is missing**

The CPI tracks what a fixed basket of goods and services costs each month and turns it into an index. The 12-month change compares this October's index with last October's. There is no last October. During the 2025 government shutdown, which ran Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, BLS stopped collecting prices, carried September's forward to fill the gap and never published most October 2025 indexes.

BLS laid out the plan in a shutdown FAQ last updated Sept. 16. Bloomberg reported Monday that the October report would leave out both annual figures, [Quartz said](https://qz.com/bls-skip-12-month-cpi-october-inflation-report-110926).

**Monthly figures still come out**

Economists in the Dow Jones survey expect prices rose 0.3% in October and core 0.2%, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/october-cpi-report-2026-inflation.html). September's gains were 0.6% and 0.3%. Energy prices were up 20.4% over the year to September, and gasoline alone made up more than half of September's monthly rise, BLS said.

Fed officials are already talking about prices. "We've got to come to terms with this cost-side and inflation-side failure," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Monday, per CNBC.

Bitcoin traded near $75,190 at 5:55 p.m. ET, up 1.1% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

Any October annual rate quoted Tuesday will be someone else's calculation, not a BLS figure. The November report is scheduled for Dec. 10.

articles.title: NYSE Picks Avalanche Ledger to Clear Its Planned Tokenized Stock Venue
articles.excerpt: Avalanche will run the ledger behind the clearing firm for an NYSE-affiliated trading system planned for 24/7 trading. It still needs regulatory approval.
articles.body_md:
The New York Stock Exchange has picked Avalanche to supply the core ledger for the clearing firm behind its planned tokenized stock venue, [Avalanche said in a blog post](https://www.avalanche.com/about/blog/wall-streets-next-chapter-is-being-built-on-avalanche) on Monday, Nov. 9. The NYSE flagged the deal in its [pre-market update](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/avalanche-to-support-nyses-affiliated-upcoming-digital-ats-nyse-content-update-302933387.html) the same morning.

The venue will be an alternative trading system (ATS), a privately run market that trades securities under SEC rules without being a full exchange. Neither company gave a launch date, and the venue still needs regulators to sign off.

**Where the blockchain sits**

Trading a stock has two halves. First, an engine matches a buyer with a seller. Then comes clearing and settlement, the step where shares and cash actually change owners, with a clearing firm standing between the two sides until it's done.

That second half is the part moving onto Avalanche. The NYSE's [January announcement](https://ir.theice.com/press/news-details/2026/The-New-York-Stock-Exchange-Develops-Tokenized-Securities-Platform/) from parent Intercontinental Exchange said the platform would pair its Pillar matching engine with blockchain-based post-trade systems, aiming for 24/7 trading, instant settlement, orders sized in dollars and funding in stablecoins. It also said tokenized shareholders would keep dividends and voting rights.

According to Avalanche, Dennis Lee, the NYSE's head of digital issuance, said the settlement ledger had to be fast, reliable, predictable in cost and able to control who takes part. [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/382833/nyse-avalanche-settle-tokenized-stock-platform) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/09/nyse-picks-avalanche-to-settle-tokenized-stocks-amid-wall-street-s-blockchain-race) also reported that the venue is designed to accept stocks issued on other blockchains.

**What the posts leave out**

Neither the Avalanche post nor the NYSE update gives fees, the name of the clearing firm, trading volumes or a timetable. AVAX, Avalanche's token, traded at $8.73 at 11:55 a.m. ET, up 6.9% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/avalanche).

*In our opinion: the bigger story is which layer moved. Tokenized funds such as BlackRock's BUIDL already sit on Avalanche, Avalanche says, but this puts a blockchain under the step where ownership changes hands for an NYSE venue. The document worth waiting for is the regulatory filing, because that's where fees, the clearing firm and a start date have to show up.*

articles.title: PNC Lets Corporate Clients Take USDC Payments, Paid Out in Dollars
articles.excerpt: The pilot runs on Coinbase's payment tools and Ethereum. PNC hasn't named the clients taking part, the price, or when it might open more widely.
articles.body_md:
PNC Bank's corporate clients can now get paid in USDC and find U.S. dollars in their account. The Pittsburgh bank [announced the pilot](https://pnc.mediaroom.com/2026-11-09-PNC-Bank-Launches-Incoming-Stablecoin-Payments-for-Corporate-and-Institutional-Banking-Clients) on Monday, Nov. 9, built on Coinbase's payment products.

For a business with customers or suppliers abroad, it's a way to accept a digital dollar without holding crypto. Incoming USDC on Ethereum is converted 1-to-1 into dollars and deposited into a designated PNC account, the bank said.

**How the payment works**

USDC is a stablecoin, a token meant to hold a steady $1 value. Its issuer, Circle, calls it "a fully reserved digital dollar" on its [USDC page](https://www.circle.com/usdc). A payer sends the token over a blockchain at any hour, and stablecoins can be sent and received almost instantly, Reuters noted. In PNC's setup, the client never ends up holding the token: Coinbase handles the crypto side and PNC books the dollars.

About $70.4 billion of USDC was in circulation on Monday, per [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins).

"Right now, this is about testing and learning with our clients," Tom Lang, PNC's head of Treasury Management product and operations, told [Reuters](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/4003973-pnc-to-offerstablecoin-payments-to-clients-in-coinbase-partnership). Alec Lovett, Coinbase's head of infrastructure products, said in the release that stablecoins make business payments "faster, more efficient and more global."

**Built on an older deal**

PNC first tied up with Coinbase in July 2025 and began offering spot bitcoin trading to eligible private banking clients in December, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-09-coinbase-pnc-bank-expand-partnership-with-usdc-payments-corporate-clients-436466) reported. This pilot is open only to eligible corporate and institutional clients. Neither company disclosed fees, the clients taking part or volumes.

*In our opinion: the detail worth chasing is the fee. PNC hasn't said what it charges to turn a stablecoin into a deposit, and that price decides whether a treasury team picks USDC over a wire. The pilot only covers money coming in, so the next real step to watch is whether PNC lets clients send USDC out.*

articles.title: Strategy Pays $79,012 a Coin for 1,036 Bitcoin, Above Its Own Average
articles.excerpt: More of the week's stock-sale money went to buying back STRC preferred shares: $188.3 million, against $81.9 million for bitcoin.
articles.body_md:
Strategy bought 1,036 bitcoin last week at an average of $79,012 each, pricier than the $75,456 it has paid on average for its whole stack, its [Form 8-K filed Monday](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526452693/mstr-20261109.htm) shows.

That means the newest coins are already worth less than they cost. Bitcoin traded near $74,950 at 11:55 a.m. ET on Monday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Black Mint [reported Sunday](https://blackmint.markets/news/bitcoin-below-strategy-average-cost/) that bitcoin had slipped below Strategy's average cost; the new buy nudged that average up by $5.

**The money went somewhere else first**

Strategy raised $283.8 million after commissions by selling 2,051,348 Class A shares through its at-the-market program, which lets a company sell new stock straight into the market a little at a time. Only $81.9 million of that, about 29%, bought bitcoin.

The largest slice, $188.3 million, went to buying back 1,887,464 shares of STRC, its variable-rate preferred stock. That works out to about $99.76 a share, [Unchained calculated](https://unchainedcrypto.com/strategy-buys-1036-btc-but-spends-more-repurchasing-its-preferred-stock-just-under-100/). Preferred stock gets its dividend paid before common shareholders see anything. STRC's rate is variable, and Executive Chairman Michael Saylor has said Strategy aims to keep its price between $99 and $100, Unchained reported.

The last $13.6 million went to "USD Cash," the company's general-purpose pot.

**Where the stack stands**

- Holdings: 850,364 BTC as of Nov. 8
- Total cost: $64.16 billion, including fees
- Value at $74,948 a coin: about $63.7 billion, roughly $430 million below cost
- USD Reserve for dividends and interest: $4.77 billion, after $21.1 million in preferred dividends last week

The filing reports no bitcoin sales. Strategy has $560.3 million left under its preferred buyback program.

*In our opinion: for a company built to buy bitcoin, spending more than twice as much on its own preferred shares is the line in this filing that deserves the attention. Holders of the common stock are funding both moves, and the $4.77 billion reserve is what covers the preferred dividends while bitcoin sits under cost. The 1,036 new coins began their Strategy careers about $4,000 each under water, so next Monday's 8-K will show whether the buyback pace holds.*

articles.title: Binance Pool Mines One Bitcoin Block in a Week Before Tuesday Shutdown
articles.excerpt: Miners still pointed at Binance Pool have until 2 a.m. ET Tuesday to switch. Pool Savings and Cloud Mining close at the same time.
articles.body_md:
Binance Pool found one of the 916 bitcoin blocks mined over the past week, about 0.11%, [mempool.space data](https://mempool.space/mining/pool/binancepool) showed at 6:04 a.m. ET Monday. The pool shuts at 07:00 UTC Tuesday, which is 2 a.m. ET.

Any miner still connected after that time earns nothing for the work. Binance's [Oct. 13 notice](https://tokenearly.com/announcement/6acd9ebaef4bd2e7553de33d.html) says shares submitted after the cutoff "will no longer be accepted, processed, or credited."

**How a mining pool pays**

A single machine almost never finds a block on its own. A pool combines thousands of miners' computing power, and when any of them finds a block, the reward (3.125 new bitcoin plus fees) is split by how much work each one sent. Miners can point the same machines at a different pool by changing one server address, without turning anything off.

Binance Pool's last block was No. 974,743, found at 9:15 p.m. ET on Nov. 5 with 1,353 transactions, per mempool.space. It found none in the latest 24 hours. Over its life it has mined 22,213 blocks, the same data show.

Bitcoin.com News [reported](https://news.bitcoin.com/mining/binance-pulls-plug-bitcoin-mining-after-6-year-run/) on Oct. 13 that the pool, launched in April 2020, was the ninth-largest by hashrate and was mining about three blocks a day. Binance's notice gave no reason for the closure.

**What else closes, and what to save**

Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, the Transaction Accelerator and the pool's API and alerts all end at the same cutoff. Binance tells users to redeem Pool Savings positions before then and to finish any identity checks by 23:59 UTC Tuesday so leftover rewards can be paid.

The week's block count also shows where the hashrate sits now. Foundry USA found 227 blocks, AntPool 173 and F2Pool 160, mempool.space shows. A week with one block is a small sample, and block luck swings, so it can't pin down how much computing power is still connected to Binance Pool.

Binance Pool's history pages, including payout records, stay viewable until 07:00 UTC on Nov. 24. After that, Binance says, they go offline for good.

articles.title: Galxe Shuts Quest, ID and Passport, Sets Dec. 15 Reward Deadline
articles.excerpt: Galxe says it served 36 million users. Campaigns end Dec. 5, and staked G and Smart Savings balances will get a separate claim process later.
articles.body_md:
Galxe users have until Dec. 15 to claim any campaign rewards. After that, the whole Galxe website goes read-only, the company [said on X](https://x.com/Galxe/status/2119681030609105175) at 1:38 a.m. ET Monday as it folds its team and brand into Gravity, its own blockchain.

Galxe Quest, Galxe ID, Galxe Passport and related services are being wound down. The last day to take part in any campaign is Dec. 5.

**How Galxe campaigns worked**

Galxe ran quest campaigns for crypto projects: a project posted tasks, such as making an on-chain transaction or following an account, and users who finished them earned rewards. Galxe ID and Passport handled identity and credentials behind those campaigns. The company says it served 36 million users and more than 7,700 partner projects over five-plus years.

**What stopped Monday**

Some of it ended right away. Starting Monday, Spaces (the project pages) can no longer create new campaigns, and new Galxe+ and Galxe Score subscriptions and Passport minting are closed, the post says.

Gravity, the network, keeps running, and the company said there are "no changes to the G token as part of this transition." G is the gas token on Gravity L1, [Crypto Briefing reported](https://cryptobriefing.com/galxe-consolidates-gravity-l1-quest-shutdown/).

**Some balances wait for a second notice**

Three kinds of assets are not on the December timetable: Smart Savings balances, staked G not yet withdrawn, and G held in wallets on Gravity Alpha Mainnet. Galxe says these "remain safe" and will follow a separate claim process, with details in a later post on X. It gave no date for that post.

That older network is already gone. Gravity Alpha Mainnet shut down on Nov. 1 after a bridging window that ran Oct. 23-25, Crypto Briefing reported, and Galxe had [warned users on X](https://x.com/Galxe/status/2113799196406915097) in October to move funds off the network before those deadlines.

Galxe's post does not say how many users still hold unclaimed rewards or how much those rewards are worth.

The next dates are fixed: campaigns close Dec. 5, and reward claims close Dec. 15.

articles.title: Coinbase Wins Full OCC Trust Charter for Custody, Not Deposits
articles.excerpt: The federal charter covers custody, not deposits or loans. Coinbase plans to move its New York custody business into the new bank over three years.
articles.body_md:
Coinbase now runs a national trust bank. The exchange said Monday that the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has granted final approval for Coinbase National Trust Company, turning the conditional charter it won on April 2 into a full one, [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2026/11/09/coinbase-gets-full-u-s-trust-charter-from-federal-banking-regulator) and [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/coinbase-full-us-trust-charter-occ/) reported.

For institutions that keep crypto with Coinbase, the custodian moves under a federal bank supervisor instead of relying on a New York State license alone.

**How a trust charter differs from a bank**

A national trust bank holds and safeguards assets for clients as a fiduciary, meaning it must act in their interest. It does not take retail deposits or make loans. The OCC's [April approval letter](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/interpretations-and-decisions/2026/cd1370.pdf) describes the new bank's job as digital asset custody, "primarily for institutional clients," plus letting custody customers hold and transfer cash and coins in their accounts. Cash held in custody sits in "for benefit of" accounts at other banks, the letter says.

The reports of Monday's approval don't say how many client assets the new bank will hold on day one. For scale, OCC-supervised uninsured national trust banks reported $1.7 trillion in custody and safekeeping accounts as of Dec. 31, 2025, the letter says.

**Staking stays with affiliates**

The letter sets limits. Custody clients can reach Coinbase's staking, Prime Trading and Prime Financing products, but the bank acts only as a finder: affiliates provide those services, not the bank itself. Coinbase will move the whole custody business from Coinbase Custody Trust Company, its New York-chartered trust firm, to the national bank over the three-year start-up period, according to the letter.

Coinbase's [April blog post](https://www.coinbase.com/blog/coinbase-receives-conditional-occ-approval-building-the-future-of-finance) said the company would not take retail deposits or engage in fractional reserve banking, and that its BitLicense and New York trust charter stay in place.

Ripple won its own final OCC trust approval on Oct. 26, Crypto Briefing reported.

*In our opinion: the line to watch is the three-year migration. Until the custody book actually moves, Coinbase runs two regulators' rulebooks side by side. The next checkable document is the OCC's own final-approval record, and whether it attaches conditions beyond April's.*
