articles.title: Emirates NBD's Liv Adds USDU, a Central Bank-Registered Dollar Token
articles.excerpt: Liv has close to half a million users and is waiving crypto trading fees for 90 days. UAE rules limit USDU to paying for digital assets.
articles.body_md:
Liv, the digital bank run by Emirates NBD, is adding USDU, a U.S. dollar stablecoin registered by the Central Bank of the UAE, to its app, the companies said in a [press release](https://www.zawya.com/en/press-release/companies-news/liv-by-emirates-nbd-universal-and-aquanow-to-deliver-the-first-integration-of-a-cbuae-registered-usd-backed-stablecoin-2127691) on Monday. To launch it, Liv is waiving crypto trading fees for 90 days.

Liv has close to half a million users, the release says. Its crypto service, Liv X, already runs on Aquanow, a Dubai-licensed broker that says it has processed more than $130 billion in trading volume.

**What the token can and can't do**

A stablecoin is a token meant to hold a fixed value, here $1, backed by cash held elsewhere. Under the UAE's Payment Token Services Regulation, payments for digital assets in the country can only be made in regular money or a registered foreign payment token, [Universal said](https://www.universal.ae/news/universal-launches-uaes-first-central-bank-registered-usd-stablecoin) when it launched USDU on Jan. 29. USDU was the first token registered that way.

The flip side: USDU "may not be used for general payment purposes in the UAE," Universal's launch notice says. Monday's release repeats that it is not a general-purpose domestic payment instrument. In practice, it is a dollar balance for buying and selling crypto.

**Who holds the dollars**

Universal, the ADGM-regulated issuer, says each token is backed 1:1 by dollars in onshore accounts at Emirates NBD and Mashreq, with monthly attestations by an outside accounting firm. That puts Emirates NBD on both ends: it safeguards part of the reserves and now sells the token to its own app customers, [tbreak reported](https://tbreak.com/liv-usdu-stablecoin-uae/).

Rohit Garg, Emirates NBD's chief digital officer for retail banking, said in the release that USDU gives customers a "secure, transparent and regulated bridge to digital assets" inside their everyday banking app.

The release does not say when USDU goes live in the app, what fees apply after the 90 days, or whether users can send it to outside wallets. It also gives no figure for how many USDU tokens exist.

*In our opinion: Emirates NBD now sits on both sides of this token, holding part of the reserves and selling USDU in its own app, which makes Universal's monthly attestations the document worth reading. Monday's release gives no supply figure, so the next attestation is the place to check how many tokens exist. The 90-day fee holiday is generous; the more telling number arrives on day 91.*

articles.title: China's Producer Prices Rise 5.7% While Consumer Inflation Cools
articles.excerpt: Coal mining prices jumped 36.6% from a year earlier while food fell 2.9%. Beijing also kept its extra 24% tariff on U.S. goods suspended for two more months.
articles.body_md:
China's factory-gate prices rose 5.7% in October from a year earlier, the National Bureau of Statistics said at 9:30 a.m. Beijing time Monday (8:30 p.m. ET Sunday). Consumer inflation went the other way, slowing to 0.7%.

The producer figure beat the 5.3% that economists polled by Reuters expected, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/china-wholesale-inflation-rises-consumer.html), and was the fastest pace since June 2022. It was the third month in a row of faster gains. The bureau said the rate widened 0.7 percentage point from September, which puts September at 5.0%.

**What the producer index measures**

The producer price index, or PPI, tracks what Chinese factories charge when goods first leave the plant. The bureau surveys prices for more than 1,300 product categories across 41 industries. Read next to consumer prices, it shows where costs are building inside supply chains, from raw materials to finished goods.

**Coal and oil did most of the lifting**

Mining prices were up 27.9% from a year earlier and raw materials 11.6%, the [bureau's PPI release](https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfbhjd/202611/t20261109_1965794.html) shows. Coal mining rose 36.6%. Oil and gas extraction rose 35.0%. Prices factories paid for their own inputs climbed 7.9%. Chief statistician Dong Lijuan [said](https://www1.xinhuanet.com/fortune/20261109/decb1630fe0f4b03b1eedaed46676cc1/c.html) higher international energy prices drove most of October's 0.7% monthly rise.

Shoppers saw little of it. Food prices fell 2.9% from a year earlier, and core CPI, which strips out food and energy, eased to 0.8% from 1.0%. Economists polled by Reuters had expected headline CPI of 0.8%, CNBC reported.

**Beijing keeps the 24% tariff on hold**

The same day, China's Customs Tariff Commission [said](https://gss.mof.gov.cn/gzdt/zhengcefabu/202611/t20261109_4004260.htm) it will keep its extra 24% tariff on U.S. goods suspended for two more months from 1:01 p.m. Tuesday Beijing time, while a 10% extra tariff stays in place, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/china-extends-suspension-of-24-tariff-on-us-imports-for-two-months-5010427). Mainland China's CSI 300 index rose 0.56% after the inflation data, per CNBC.

Bitcoin was down 1.3% over 24 hours at $74,762 at 11:56 p.m. ET, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) data show.

*In our opinion: the number that matters is the five-point gap. Chinese factories are charging 5.7% more while shoppers pay 0.7% more, and the bureau's own breakdown puts most of the factory jump on coal and oil. The next checks are China's November figures and early January, when the two-month tariff pause runs out.*

articles.excerpt: Strategy's 849,327 BTC cost $64.08 billion and were worth about $63.4 billion Sunday evening. Reuters said bitcoin hit its lowest level since August.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell to about $74,650 on Sunday evening, below the $75,451 average price Strategy has paid for its coins. On those figures, the company's bitcoin stack is worth about $675 million less than it cost.

Strategy's [Nov. 2 filing with the SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526442707/mstr-20261102.htm) shows it held 849,327 BTC as of Nov. 1, bought for $64.08 billion including fees and expenses. At $74,653 per coin at 6:04 p.m. ET, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), those coins were worth about $63.4 billion. The filing is the latest holdings count we could find, so the real total may differ if Strategy bought more this week.

**How an average cost works**

Strategy has bought bitcoin in many batches at different prices. Its "average purchase price" is the total spent divided by the total coins held. When the market price sits below that number, the holding is worth less than was paid for it. That's a paper position: nothing is lost or locked in unless coins are sold, and the filing reports no sales.

**The move behind it**

Bitcoin was down 1.4% over 24 hours and 9.7% over 30 days at 6:04 p.m. ET, CoinGecko data show. [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/forex-news/cryptocurrencies-slide-to-twomonth-lows-after-us-midterms-5010335) that bitcoin dipped to $73,708 in late Sunday trade, the lowest since August, and that ether fell to $2,223. Reuters attributed the drop to investor worry that a Democratic-controlled Congress will toughen crypto regulation, and to the roughly $6 billion Binance theft.

At $73,708, the same 849,327 coins would be worth about $62.6 billion, or $1.5 billion below cost.

The last cost basis Strategy published was $80,846 per coin for the 811 BTC it added during the week of Oct. 26. Those newest coins were already above the market price.

*In our opinion: the line to check is Strategy's next weekly filing, which will show whether Strategy bought this week and at what price, which moves the $75,451 figure, even if only a little. A company that has put $64 billion into one asset keeps its scorecard in public, and this week the scorecard reads slightly red.*

articles.title: LNbits Tells Every Server Operator to Shut Down Pending Patches
articles.excerpt: The Lightning account system's developers say fixes should land in 24 to 48 hours. LNbits has not named the flaw or said how many servers were hit.
articles.body_md:
LNbits told everyone running its software to stop their servers immediately on Sunday, saying a wave of attacks had left it with security patches still to push. Contributor Ben Arc said the fixes should be merged and available within 24 to 48 hours.

The project's [8:56 a.m. ET post on X](https://x.com/lnbits/status/2119428804951048237) asked users to stop servers "IMMEDIATELY" and said, "it's better to err on the side of caution." Arc [added three minutes later](https://x.com/arcbtc/status/2119429503667642816) that operators should pass the warning on to anyone who might be running an instance. At 12:18 p.m. ET, LNbits [said](https://x.com/lnbits/status/2119479738783629384) it had switched off every instance on its own hosted service as a precaution and expected services to resume within 24 hours.

**From one extension to every server**

The warning widened through the morning. At 7:33 a.m. ET, LNbits had [asked operators](https://x.com/lnbits/status/2119408009700937798) with its Paywall extension enabled to turn it off while it investigated "a potential bug." The 8:56 a.m. post covered every server, with or without that extension.

**How LNbits works**

LNbits is open-source software that sits on top of a Lightning node and lets one operator give separate wallets to many users, with add-on extensions for things like paywalls and tipping. Because each server is connected to a node holding real bitcoin, a flaw in LNbits can reach that money. That's why the project is asking operators to stop servers rather than wait for a patch.

**A loss one operator reported**

Kevin Ravensberg, who runs the LNbits server behind the BitTipBot Telegram tipping bot, said newly created accounts withdrew 2,285,545 sats, about 0.023 bitcoin, from his server on Sunday before he stopped it, [Bitcoin.com News reported](https://news.bitcoin.com/security/lightning-network-security-scare-forces-lnbits-servers-offline/). It said he plans to cover the bot's users himself. We could not independently confirm the figure.

**What isn't known**

LNbits has not said what the vulnerabilities are, whether the Paywall bug is among them, how many servers were attacked, or how much was taken in total. Its latest tagged release on [GitHub](https://github.com/lnbits/lnbits/releases) is v1.6.2 from Sept. 18, and no new security advisory was listed when we checked at 6 p.m. ET.

Operators who stopped their servers should keep them off until a fixed release is published and LNbits says it is safe to restart.

articles.title: Binance Reopens HYPE and APT Withdrawals, Four of Six Still Pending
articles.excerpt: Binance said Friday it aimed to reopen six tokens by the end of next week. INJ, PLASMA, NEAR and LTC weren't on Sunday's list, 10 days after the $6.3 billion theft.
articles.body_md:
Binance reopened withdrawals for Hyperliquid's HYPE and Aptos' APT tokens at 3:52 a.m. ET Sunday, the exchange said in a [post on X](https://x.com/binance/status/2119352231732580574), ten days after the Oct. 29 theft of about $6.3 billion.

Those are two of the six tokens Binance named on Friday. In a [Nov. 6 post](https://x.com/binance/status/2118657118014496819), it said it was working to reopen HYPE, INJ, APT, PLASMA, NEAR and LTC "by end of next week," along with every token on networks already restored, including BSC, Ethereum, Arbitrum and Optimism.

**Four named tokens are still waiting**

Sunday's update lists HYPE and APT as new. It doesn't mention INJ, PLASMA, NEAR or LTC, and Binance hasn't given a date for them beyond Friday's target.

How does a withdrawal reopen one token at a time? When a customer withdraws, the exchange sends coins from its own wallets onto a specific blockchain. Each network has its own wallets, addresses and signing setup, so each route has to be checked separately before money moves again. That's why Binance's updates list assets network by network (five Ethereum stablecoins, including RLUSD and USD1, came back earlier).

**The money behind the restart**

Binance's [Recovery Update #7](https://x.com/binance/status/2118001921252347938) on Nov. 4 said 98% of the stolen assets were covered and came with an expanded proof-of-reserves snapshot. That is a published tally of what the exchange holds against what customers are owed at a single moment. Binance has said users won't bear the losses.

The FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group for the attack, an allegation Pyongyang has denied, [Reuters reported](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/binance-cfo-kaiser-ng-steps-down-justin-yek-named-new-finance-chief-6533351).

HYPE was at $76.86 at 12:02 p.m. ET, down 0.6% in 24 hours, and APT was at $0.58, down 2.9%, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: the count that matters now is four. Binance set its own deadline on Friday for INJ, PLASMA, NEAR and LTC, so the end of this coming week is the date to check. Customers holding those tokens on the exchange are still waiting on the one service a reserve snapshot can't replace: getting their coins out.*

articles.title: Keplr Says Some Emptied Balances Reflect Web3Auth Rescue Moves
articles.excerpt: Web3Auth posted the addresses holding rescued Keplr funds on 11 networks plus eight EVM chains. Neither firm has given a loss figure or a count of affected accounts.
articles.body_md:
Some Keplr wallets created with Google or Apple login may already show a reduced or empty balance because of rescue transfers, Keplr said in a [post on X](https://x.com/keplrwallet/status/2119117067500806350). At 1:23 a.m. ET Sunday, Web3Auth published the [recovery addresses](https://x.com/Web3Auth/status/2119314958236401922) holding those funds.

That matters for anyone who opened a Keplr wallet with a social login and saw coins leave. Web3Auth said some of its transfers "have been mistaken for attacker activity."

**How a rescue transfer works**

Web3Auth said Saturday that it and its partners had begun "whitehat recovery," aimed at wallets that were exposed but not yet drained, "utilizing the same path of the original attacker." In plain terms, defenders used the same weakness to move coins out first, into wallets they control, so an attacker couldn't reach them. Keplr described the flaw as a Web3Auth "infrastructure vulnerability leading to private key breach." Web3Auth runs the login service Keplr uses for Google and Apple sign-ins.

The list covers 11 networks, including Cosmos Hub, Osmosis, Celestia, Injective, dYdX and Noble, plus one address used on eight EVM chains, the networks that run Ethereum-style software. Web3Auth said it will add addresses as they are verified.

**What users were told to do**

Wallets made with a recovery phrase or a hardware device aren't affected, Keplr said. Social-login users were told not to send new funds to those accounts and to move any remaining liquid assets to a phrase or hardware wallet. Staked and locked tokens take longer to secure, Keplr said.

Neither company has said how many accounts were hit, how much was taken by the attacker or how much was moved to safety. Keplr said it is working with Web3Auth on a way for users to check whether their account is affected, and both said to trust only their official accounts and ignore "recovery" offers by DM.

*In our opinion: the address list is the most useful thing either company has published so far, because it lets users tell a rescue from a theft on-chain. The missing numbers are the next test. Until Web3Auth says how much it holds and how users get it back, affected holders can see where their coins went but not when they return.*

articles.title: Stablecoin Supply Falls to $292 Billion, Lowest in More Than a Year
articles.excerpt: Tether's USDT shed $2.8 billion in a week and Circle's USDC $1.2 billion as total supply slid for a fifth week, DefiLlama data show.
articles.body_md:
Stablecoin supply fell to $292.4 billion on Sunday, its lowest level since Sept. 24, 2025, [DefiLlama data](https://defillama.com/stablecoins) show. That's $6.6 billion less than on Oct. 31.

The slide has run for five weeks. DefiLlama's total stood at $307.9 billion on Oct. 7 and peaked at $315.5 billion on May 17, so about $23 billion has left the market since spring.

**Tether and Circle took most of the week's drop**

- Tether's USDT: down $2.8 billion in seven days, to $176.8 billion
- Circle's USDC: down $1.2 billion, to $70.6 billion
- World Liberty's USD1: down $430 million, to $3.45 billion

[CoinGecko's figures](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/tether) line up. USDT's market value slipped from $180.0 billion on Nov. 1 to $176.9 billion early Sunday, and [USDC's](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/usd-coin) went from $71.7 billion to $70.5 billion.

A few coins grew. Ethena's USDe added $431 million, to $4.93 billion, and Ripple's RLUSD added $274 million, to $2.69 billion, per DefiLlama.

**How a stablecoin shrinks**

A stablecoin is a token built to stay worth $1. Big issuers such as Tether and Circle mint new tokens when approved customers send in dollars, and burn them when customers cash out. Trading coins back and forth doesn't change the count. Supply falls only when more money is redeemed than deposited.

That makes the total a rough gauge of how many dollars are parked inside crypto, ready to trade or lend.

The data don't show who redeemed or why.

Prices barely moved on Sunday. Bitcoin sat near $75,820 at 5:55 a.m. ET, down 0.1% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko, after U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $411.9 million on Friday, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/) data show.

*In our opinion: the weekly change tells the story here. Five straight weeks of shrinking supply means more dollars are walking out than walking in, and USDT and USDC account for about $4 billion of this week's exits. The check-in worth making is Nov. 15, when a sixth weekly reading will show whether the exits slow or keep going.*

articles.title: OKX Asks Users to Stop Direct MEXC Transfers Ahead of FinCEN Cutoff
articles.excerpt: OKX CEO Star Xu said MEXC-linked funds get sanctions-style checks and possible freezes. FinCEN's 30-day clock hasn't started; OKX isn't waiting.
articles.body_md:
OKX founder and CEO Star Xu asked customers on Saturday to stop sending money straight from MEXC to OKX, two days after FinCEN's order against MEXC. "Please avoid transferring funds directly from MEXC to OKX," Xu [wrote on X](https://x.com/star_okx/status/2119203186074599424) at 5:59 p.m. ET.

Xu said OKX treats FinCEN special measures "with a level of caution similar to sanctions." Funds tied to affected platforms may be frozen, he wrote, with the related accounts open to further investigation. FinCEN allowed a 30-day transition, but OKX tightened its controls without waiting.

**A user's 860 USDT sat in review**

Xu was answering an [X user](https://x.com/HoppinsKarlz/status/2119017596796153998) who said deposits from their own MEXC account, 848.8 USDT on Tron and 11.7 USDT on Ethereum, were held for risk review after OKX flagged a "potentially high-risk address." [PANews](https://www.panews.io/articles/01a1b8ad-8362-7203-b2b9-3ffe90e0dbb4) and [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/okx-star-xu-avoid-mexc-transfers/) also reported Xu's remarks.

How does a deposit get stuck? Exchanges run incoming transfers through analytics tools that score the sending addresses. If a source is tied to a flagged platform, the deposit is parked while compliance staff ask where the money came from. FinCEN's order itself only bars covered U.S. financial institutions from moving funds to or from MEXC Global. OKX's step is its own policy.

Treasury [alleges](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0685) MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit transactions from May 2021 to May 2026, as Black Mint reported Friday. The ban starts 30 days after the order is published in the Federal Register. It was not on the Register's [public inspection list](https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/current) late Saturday ET.

**MEXC says it is operating normally**

MEXC said in a [statement](https://www.mexc.com/announcements/article/statement-regarding-fincen-s-november-6-order-17827791539626) that it is reviewing the order with its legal and compliance teams, that "user assets remain secure," and that it has begun an independent review of its anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls. CEO Vugar Usi said Saturday that deposits and withdrawals had not been suspended, [The Crypto Times reported](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/11/07/mexc-ceo-says-exchange-remains-live-after-us-treasury-ban/).

Xu did not say how many accounts or how much money OKX has held.

*In our opinion: the legal clock hasn't started, yet a major offshore exchange is already handling MEXC money the way it handles sanctioned money. That puts the first cost on ordinary MEXC customers, and Xu's own post allowed that a user hit by it could be "an innocent user caught up in this situation." Watch for the Federal Register notice, which starts the 30 days, and for any other exchange that posts similar deposit rules before it lands.*

articles.title: Sky's Savings Vault Sheds $571 Million in a Day at a 3.80% Rate
articles.excerpt: USDS supply also fell $805 million on the week to $5.59 billion, DefiLlama shows. Sky's savings rate never moved, and no one has said who withdrew.
articles.body_md:
Holders pulled about 571 million USDS out of Sky's savings vault in the 24 hours to 7 p.m. ET Friday, cutting deposits about 13% to 3.95 billion, [Aavescan's](https://aavescan.com/rates/sky-susds) daily reads of the vault contract show. The rate paid on those deposits stayed at 3.80%.

The drop shows up in the wider numbers too. Sky's total value locked fell to about $4.43 billion early Sunday from $5.23 billion a week earlier, and USDS circulating supply slid to $5.59 billion from $6.40 billion, [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/protocol/sky) data show. A direct read of the vault contract by Black Mint at about midnight ET Sunday returned 3.98 billion USDS.

**How the savings vault works**

USDS is Sky's dollar stablecoin, the successor to DAI. Holders who deposit USDS get sUSDS, a token that grows in value at the Sky Savings Rate. The rate is set by Sky governance and paid from the protocol's surplus, [TokenPost reported](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/technology/47289), after governance raised it to 3.80% in October. On-chain data from [Chartegy](https://chartegy.com/data/series/SKY_SAVINGS_RATE) show it unchanged since at least Oct. 26.

Withdrawing swaps sUSDS back into USDS (the coins come out of the vault, they don't disappear). That alone doesn't shrink supply. Supply falls only when USDS is redeemed or burned, which is why the two figures moved by different amounts.

**Who moved the money is not known**

Neither data source identifies the wallets behind Friday's withdrawal. Sky's main X accounts had not posted about it through Saturday. On Nov. 6, the [Sky Ecosystem account](https://x.com/SkyEcosystem/status/2118697883121914148) posted about a $100 million sUSDS allocation from Galaxy.

Vault deposits had held between about $4.48 billion and $4.58 billion from Oct. 29 through Nov. 5, Aavescan's snapshots show. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/sky-tvl-falls-15-in-a-week-as-usds-supply-contracts) also reported the weekly decline.

*In our opinion: when an eighth of a savings vault walks out and the rate doesn't twitch, the rate probably wasn't the reason. The useful number now is concentration: if a handful of wallets made Friday's exit, the vault's transaction log will show it before any statement does. Watch whether USDS supply keeps sliding from $5.59 billion this week, because that figure counts dollars leaving the Sky system altogether.*

articles.title: Binance Names Justin Yek CFO Nine Days After $6.3B Hack
articles.excerpt: Co-CEO Yi He said the handover was planned over six months. Yek was vice president of finance at Airwallex; Ng had been CFO since January 2022.
articles.body_md:
Binance said Saturday that finance chief Kaiser Ng is leaving after more than five years, with Justin Yek taking over as CFO. The change comes nine days after hackers took about $6.3 billion from the exchange on Oct. 29, [Reuters reported](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/binance-cfo-kaiser-ng-steps-down-justin-yek-named-new-finance-chief-6533351).

The company tied the move to a plan, not the breach. "Kaiser Ng has decided to pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance, with a transition plan implemented over the last half year," co-CEO Yi He said in a statement carried by Reuters. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/07/binance-cfo-is-leaving-to-pursue-a-new-venture-after-6-3-billion-hack/), citing Bloomberg, reported the same quote.

**Yek comes from a payments company**

Yek was most recently vice president of finance at Airwallex, a payments firm, according to Reuters. Ng has been Binance's CFO since January 2022 and worked at Kraken before that, Reuters said, citing his LinkedIn profile.

Why does the seat matter right now? A chief financial officer runs a company's money: its books, cash, reporting and the reserves that back what it owes. At an exchange, that last part is customer balances. Binance has said it will fully reimburse users hit by the theft, and TechCrunch quoted the company: "These losses will not be passed on to users." Covering a loss that size from company funds is a finance-office job.

**What the statement leaves out**

Neither report gives Ng's last day, says what his new venture is, or explains why the handover was announced now. Binance's statement, as quoted, does not mention the hack.

Binance has said the attack began months earlier with malware hidden in software downloads and fake job offers aimed at its engineers. The FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group, an allegation Pyongyang has denied, Reuters reported.

*In our opinion: the timing will draw questions, and Binance has answered only one of them: it says the plan predates the breach by six months. The open item is the reimbursement bill, which now lands on a new CFO's desk in his first weeks. The next thing to watch is any Binance update on how much of that reimbursement has been paid, and from which funds.*

articles.title: Treasury Sanctions 8 Canadian Firms Over Alleged Iran Crypto Links
articles.excerpt: OFAC designated eight Ontario and B.C. money services businesses under E.O. 13902. Treasury says they swapped rials and other cash into digital assets for Iran-linked flows.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control on Friday designated eight Canadian money services businesses that it says help move value for Iran by exchanging Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets, according to a [Treasury press release](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0686) and the matching [OFAC SDN update](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261106).

U.S. persons generally may not deal with the firms. Property they hold in the United States is blocked. The action sits under Executive Order 13902, which targets Iran's digital-asset sector among other parts of its economy.

**What OFAC says the firms did**

Treasury alleges the companies, based in Ontario and British Columbia, gave sanctioned Iranian actors a channel to move money abroad. Named firms include Diverse Trade Inc. (Million Exchange), Amin Exchange entities, NIA Nations Currency Ltd., Farah Exchange, CCC Inc., B Galaxy Inc. (Cryptoyal) and Darvish Exchange. OFAC says addresses tied to several of them transacted with sanctioned Iranian exchanges such as Nobitex, Wallex, Ramzinex, Bitpin and Shelbit, and in some cases with addresses linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

A money services business in this context is a firm that changes cash or currencies and, here, often converts those funds into crypto for cross-border transfer. OFAC's list update posts specific TRON addresses for several of the designated entities.

Treasury also says some of the firms handled drug proceeds for Ryan Wedding, a former Olympic snowboarder who was apprehended in January 2026 and who, OFAC alleges, used Canadian exchangers to turn bulk cash into digital assets sent abroad. CBC News reported Friday that it contacted Wedding's lawyer for comment. Public responses from the eight firms were not posted on their sites by midday Saturday ET.

The designations continue Operation Economic Outcast, launched in August, and follow earlier OFAC actions against Iranian exchanges including Nobitex and Shelbit. FinCEN and Canada's FINTRAC coordinated on the package, Treasury said.

Friday's [OFAC update](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261106) lists the eight entities and their TRON addresses on the SDN List. The next check for desks screening counterparties is whether those wallets appear in weekend settlement flows.

articles.title: Binance France Closes Accounts Dec. 31, Fees From Nov. 29
articles.excerpt: A client email sets a Dec. 31 closure after Binance missed MiCA. Idle balances face 0.025% or 10 USDC a month from the Nov. 29 calculation day.
articles.body_md:
Binance France will close every customer account on Dec. 31, 2026, and will start charging monthly fees on Nov. 29 for balances that remain, according to an email to French clients that [Cryptoast published Friday](https://cryptoast.fr/binance-annonce-cloture-comptes-utilisateurs-francais-31-decembre/).

Deposits are already blocked. Withdrawals still work. Accounts emptied before the Nov. 29 "calculation day" pay nothing, the email says.

**How the wind-down works**

The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation, or MiCA, required EU crypto service providers to hold authorization by June 30, 2026. Binance France did not secure that license. French outlet Cryptoast and Bitcoin.com News both quote the same notice: because of an "orderly cessation of activities," accounts close as of Dec. 31, and assets left behind may be converted, transferred or otherwise handled under Binance's terms.

From Nov. 29, any open Binance France account is charged 0.025% of its balance or 10 USDC, whichever is higher. The first collection is due within three days of Nov. 29; a second is expected after Dec. 24. Fees come from USDC first, then other crypto. If the balance is smaller than the fee, Binance takes what is left.

On a $500 balance, the 10 USDC floor is a 2% hit each month. Only balances above about $40,000 pay the percentage rate instead. Cryptoast says clients can close the account at any time.

Trading for French residents had already ended after the July 1 MiCA transition. The Dec. 31 date ends the withdraw-only window. Neither Binance's global blog nor France's AMF had posted a matching English press release by midday Saturday ET; the client email remains the primary notice.

*In our opinion: the clock for holders is the Nov. 29 calculation day. Accounts emptied before then skip both fee collections. After Dec. 31, leftover assets fall under Binance's terms language; a dated AMF handling schedule has not been posted.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $1.28 Billion in Worst Week Since June
articles.excerpt: Four of five sessions were red. BlackRock's IBIT alone lost about $1.21 billion; Fidelity's FBTC finished the week about $93 million ahead.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.28 billion from Nov. 2 through Nov. 6, their heaviest week of outflows since the week ended June 26, according to Farside Investors and SoSoValue data reported Saturday.

That is more than six times the $202.4 million that left the prior week. Ether ETFs lost another $365.3 million, extending a six-week outflow streak, SoSoValue shows.

A spot bitcoin ETF holds bitcoin and issues shares that trade on a stock exchange. When more shares are redeemed than created, the fund sells bitcoin and the day prints as a net outflow. Those daily prints are a public read on whether U.S. fund buyers are adding or cutting exposure.

**IBIT led the exits; FBTC finished green**

Farside's daily totals add to about $1.28 billion for the week: $398.6 million out Monday, $115.6 million Tuesday, $74.6 million in Wednesday, then $430.2 million and $411.9 million out Thursday and Friday. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for roughly $1.21 billion of the week's bitcoin-fund losses, including $403 million on Friday alone. Fidelity's FBTC took in about $93.1 million for the week, including a $236.7 million Wednesday inflow that partly offset later redemptions. Same product class, opposite week: IBIT bled, FBTC finished ahead.

SoSoValue puts Solana ETF outflows near $26.3 million and Hyperliquid products near $15.6 million for the same five sessions. Bitcoin traded near $75,690 at about noon ET Saturday, down 0.3% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

The prior worse week ended June 26, when the bitcoin funds shed about $1.79 billion. This week's total ranks among the largest weekly draws since the products launched in January 2024.

*In our opinion: the number worth chasing next is Monday's print after the U.S. close. A second straight heavy week would deepen the November hole; a quieter day would show whether Thursday and Friday were the bulk of the exit. Inside the $1.28 billion, Fidelity finished about $93 million ahead while IBIT alone accounted for roughly $1.21 billion of the loss.*

articles.title: Bitquery Traces $4.06M USDT Drains Across 365 TRON Wallets
articles.excerpt: Forty-three collector wallets shared one fee payer from Oct. 5 to Nov. 4. CertiK separately warned unpatched iPhones face DarkSword kit risk.
articles.body_md:
Blockchain data firm [Bitquery](https://bitquery.io/investigations/iphone-wallet-drain-tron-usdt) says at least $4.06 million in USDT left 365 TRON wallets between Oct. 5 and Nov. 4, routed to 43 short-lived collector addresses that all drew network fees from one common fee wallet.

The firm verified the on-chain figures on Nov. 5. It also counted 137,688 TRX taken from those addresses and at least $103,000 more emptied from 65 wallets on eight other chains, including Ethereum and BNB Chain.

**How the drains worked**

On TRON, moving USDT costs a fee paid in TRX. Bitquery says the fee wallet first sent a few TRX to a target address, then the whole USDT balance left for a collector within seconds, and leftover TRX followed. That pattern is how investigators linked the collectors. A shared fee wallet ties the money trail together; Bitquery says it does not by itself prove one operator controlled every theft.

Bitquery matched one Oct. 15 case, 16,428 USDT plus TRX 12 seconds later, to a published account from an iPhone owner who said they opened a video in Safari and tapped an ad. For the other addresses, the firm says the chain does not show which phone or wallet app held the seed phrase. It found no evidence of a flaw inside Trust Wallet or other apps; the risk it describes sits in device malware that searches phones for recovery phrases.

**Separate DarkSword warning**

Separately on Friday, auditor [CertiK](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/11/06/certik-warns-darksword-ios-exploit-can-target-crypto-wallets/) warned that a newer DarkSword iOS exploit kit is being used against unpatched iPhones, and that opening a malicious site in Safari can be enough. CertiK said the kit can pull Keychain data and search Photos and the Notes app for seed phrases, and listed MetaMask, Trust Wallet, Phantom, Exodus and Coinbase among apps whose on-device data can be targeted. It advised installing the latest iOS update, keeping seed phrases offline, and enabling Lockdown Mode for higher-risk users.

Bitquery's totals are a floor: only full-balance USDT empties tied to the fee wallet are counted. Most devices behind Bitquery's count remain unidentified. Bitquery has not attributed the full $4.06 million total to DarkSword alone.

*In our opinion: the next check for holders is the phone OS version and where the seed phrase lives. An updated iOS build and an offline phrase close the door these reports describe.*

articles.title: Keplr Pauses Google and Apple Login After Unauthorized Transfers
articles.excerpt: Web3Auth put its Login Service into maintenance citing a security incident. Seed-phrase and hardware wallets are not affected, Keplr said.
articles.body_md:
Keplr paused Google and Apple login early Saturday after it received reports of unauthorized transfers from some accounts created that way, the Cosmos wallet said in a [post on X](https://x.com/keplrwallet/status/2118926087615045807) timed at 04:38 UTC.

Recovery-phrase and hardware-wallet accounts are not affected in Keplr's initial assessment. Social-login users were told not to send new funds to those accounts and not to re-import or recreate them while the probe runs. Google and Apple login stay paused.

**What social login does**

Social login lets a user open a wallet with a Google or Apple account instead of writing down a recovery phrase. Keplr routes that flow through Web3Auth, a Consensys-owned login provider that rebuilds a private key when a valid login token is checked. Seed-phrase wallets never pass through that service, which matches Keplr's first split: phrase and hardware accounts clear, Google and Apple accounts may not be.

**Web3Auth and MetaMask's read**

Web3Auth's [status page](https://status.web3auth.io/events/maintenance/461) says it placed the Login Service into maintenance at 05:53 UTC Saturday "due to a security incident," with a precautionary pause until the service is restored. In a [MetaMask Builder forum note](https://builder.metamask.io/t/a-security-incident-with-web3auth-embedded-wallets/3663), Web3Auth said the issue affects its Embedded Wallet services used by some third parties and that an initial check found no evidence MetaMask users were hit.

Neither Keplr nor Web3Auth has published a count of accounts, a dollar loss, a chain list or a cause. Keplr said updates will come only from its official account. It told readers to ignore direct messages and links that offer "recovery."

*In our opinion: the open question is still size. Until Keplr or Web3Auth posts a loss figure and a cause, the practical check for readers is whether any funds sit in a Google- or Apple-created Keplr account and whether those balances stay put overnight.*

articles.title: India ED Searches CoinDCX, Delta Over Alleged FEMA Violations
articles.excerpt: Searches hit three Bengaluru sites Nov. 4-5. Both firms say they cooperated; CoinDCX called it a routine enquiry, Moneycontrol reported.
articles.body_md:
India's Enforcement Directorate searched three Bengaluru premises linked to CoinDCX and Delta Exchange on Nov. 4 and 5 over alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, the agency said on Nov. 6.

The probe targets Neblio Technologies Private Limited, which operates CoinDCX, and Excelium Technologies Private Limited, which operates Delta Exchange India, [Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/ed-searches-coindcx-delta-exchange-offices-in-bengaluru-over-alleged-fema-violations-14073770.html) and [CNBC-TV18](https://www.cnbctv18.com/india/ed-searches-3-premises-linked-to-coindcx-delta-exchange-fema-case-20029339.htm) reported, citing the agency. The ED alleges the platforms offered crypto futures and options and trading in tokenised foreign stocks without authorisation for the cross-border flows involved.

**What the agency alleges**

According to the ED, CoinDCX users deposited Indian rupees, which the platform converted into USDT and sent to overseas exchanges including Binance, KuCoin and Gate.io to fill spot orders. The agency said those transfers ran through an account in the name of a Costa Rica-based entity it called a paper company, and that the volume ran into thousands of crores of rupees. It also alleged CoinDCX opened matching futures and options positions on overseas venues, and that some global stock futures were actually placed on Hyperliquid, a foreign decentralised platform. Delta Exchange India, the ED said, transferred hundreds of crores of rupees to overseas associates and routed a large volume of derivatives and tokenised-stock trades through CoinDCX. None of those claims has been proven in court.

**How the platforms answered**

A CoinDCX spokesperson said ED officials visited the Bengaluru office as part of a routine enquiry, that the firm cooperated fully, and that as an FIU-IND-registered entity it complies with applicable Indian laws including FEMA. Delta Exchange India said trading, deposits and withdrawals continue normally, user funds remain in Indian banks, and it does not facilitate cross-border virtual-digital-asset transfers. The ED said further investigation is underway (no charges have been filed in the reports we checked).

USDT is a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Tether. Converting rupees into USDT and sending them abroad can, under FEMA rules, count as a cross-border capital transfer that needs authorisation. That is the legal hinge the agency is testing.

*In our opinion: the hinge is whether rupee-to-USDT routes to foreign exchanges violate FEMA. India already allows domestic crypto trading under tax and FIU rules. Both firms say they are cooperating; the next checkable step is whatever the ED files or freezes next.*

articles.title: CPI, PPI and Fed Speakers Fill the Week Ahead Calendar
articles.excerpt: October CPI lands Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. ET; PPI follows Friday. Veterans Day closes U.S. markets Wednesday, per Fed and BLS calendars.
articles.body_md:
October consumer prices land Tuesday and producer prices land Friday, bookending a holiday-shortened week that also packs several Federal Reserve speakers. Bitcoin heads into it near $75,830, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) around midnight ET Saturday.

The stretch follows Friday's jobs report, which showed 165,000 hires in October, and two straight days of U.S. spot bitcoin ETF outflows totaling about $842 million on Nov. 5 and 6, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show. The next FOMC decision is Dec. 8-9, per the Fed's [meeting calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm).

## The dates

- **Monday, Nov. 9:** Markets open; Fed releases its daily H.15 selected interest rates and H.10 foreign exchange rates, per the [Fed November calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/2026-november.htm).
- **Tuesday, Nov. 10, 8:30 a.m. ET:** October Consumer Price Index and real earnings, per the [BLS November schedule](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/11_sched_list.htm). Governor Christopher J. Waller speaks on the economic outlook at 4 a.m. ET in London; Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman has economic-outlook appearances the same day, per the Fed calendar.
- **Wednesday, Nov. 11:** Veterans Day. U.S. markets are closed; Fed statistical releases scheduled for the day move to Thursday, Nov. 12, the Fed calendar says.
- **Friday, Nov. 13, 8:30 a.m. ET:** October Producer Price Index, per BLS. Vice Chair Philip N. Jefferson speaks at 7 p.m. ET on technology and productivity; Bowman discusses supervision and regulation earlier that day.

**How CPI feeds crypto**

The Consumer Price Index measures the change in prices paid by urban consumers for a basket of goods and services. A hotter-than-expected print can lift odds of further Fed rate increases, which often firm the dollar and weigh on non-yielding assets such as bitcoin. A cooler print can do the reverse. Markets price those odds in futures; Black Mint does not forecast the print.

Tuesday's CPI lands at 8:30 a.m. ET. Friday's PPI follows at the same clock. The Dec. 8-9 FOMC is the policy meeting those prints feed.

articles.title: BOJ's Ueda Says Unclear How Long 2% Inflation Will Hold
articles.excerpt: He also flagged upside risks as energy prices feed into consumer inflation into early 2027. The next BOJ decision is Dec. 18.
articles.body_md:
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said Friday that underlying inflation is around the central bank's 2% target but that it is unclear how long that equilibrium will last, speaking at an International Monetary Fund seminar in Washington.

"I think we are now in an equilibrium state. As for whether we can maintain this equilibrium for a very long time into the future, we do not know," Ueda said, according to remarks carried by [Tiger Brokers](https://www.itiger.com/news/1110023321) from the Bloomberg report of the session. [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/boj-chief-ueda-sees-some-upside-risks-inflation-6532056), citing Reuters, also reported that Ueda sees "some upside risks" to inflation as energy-related prices begin to feed into consumer prices into early next year.

**Why Japan rates matter for crypto**

When the BOJ holds policy loose relative to the Federal Reserve, the yen often weakens and global investors borrow yen to buy higher-yielding assets elsewhere, a pattern sometimes called the yen carry trade. Tighter BOJ policy can reverse that flow, pull liquidity from risk markets, and show up in bitcoin and other crypto prices. Ueda said the BOJ watches other central banks "very, very carefully" because their moves affect exchange rates, interest rates and asset prices.

He said wages are growing at a level consistent with 2% inflation, but that 2% has not yet become a social norm in Japan. The bank's job now, he said, is to keep underlying inflation anchored near the target through appropriate policy adjustments. He did not give a fresh timetable for further rate increases.

Bitcoin traded near $75,830 around midnight ET Saturday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), after U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted a $411.9 million net outflow on Nov. 6, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show.

*In our opinion: Ueda reached the target and then refused to declare victory. The next BOJ meeting on Dec. 18 is the date that will show whether "unclear how long" turns into another hike or another wait.*

articles.title: Elliptic Tracks $124M of Binance Loot Moved Into Bitcoin
articles.excerpt: About 1,650 BTC arrived from stolen altcoins by Friday morning. Roughly $3.11 billion still sits in linked wallets, Elliptic said.
articles.body_md:
Attackers who stole about $6.43 billion from Binance on Oct. 29 have converted roughly $124 million of other stolen tokens into about 1,650 bitcoin, blockchain analytics firm [Elliptic](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/how-north-korea-is-laundering-the-6-4-billion-stolen-from-binance/) said in a Friday update.

That conversion nearly doubled in a day. Elliptic's last refresh, timed at 08:45 UTC Nov. 6, put about $3.11 billion still sitting in linked addresses, mostly ether and bitcoin that have not moved. About $2.85 billion of the original haul has been frozen or seized, largely by stablecoin issuers.

**How the swaps work**

Cross-chain swap protocols such as THORChain let a wallet send one asset on one blockchain and receive another asset on a different chain, without a centralized custodian. Elliptic said most of Friday's newly converted bitcoin came from stolen XRP routed that way: about 42 million XRP, worth about $50 million, had left since Thursday afternoon, leaving about 192 million XRP, or $226 million, still held. Nearly all of the stolen Solana has already been swapped, bridged or mixed, with much of that value ending in bitcoin wallets, Elliptic wrote.

The firm has mapped more than 20,000 wallets across 16 blockchains and at least 65,000 transactions. It said only a "negligible amount" has likely been cashed out into fiat. The original 18,270 bitcoin taken from Binance, split across 19 wallets, has not moved since the theft night. The FBI has attributed the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor operation; Pyongyang has denied responsibility, [Bitcoin.com News](https://news.bitcoin.com/crypto-news/stolen-binance-bitcoin-xrp-3-1b-remains-unlaundered-elliptic/) reported, citing the attribution.

Elliptic expects remaining ether to be swapped into bitcoin in small batches before cash-out attempts through over-the-counter brokers. Binance has been reopening withdrawals in stages after the breach.

*In our opinion: Elliptic still puts cash-out at a negligible amount. The freeze that caught $2.85 billion already did the hard work; the next checkable step is whether exchanges and OTC desks stop the converted bitcoin before it leaves the chain.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $411.9 Million for a Second Straight Day
articles.excerpt: IBIT alone lost $403.0 million Friday. Ether ETFs shed $93.3 million and Solana ETFs $24.2 million the same day, Farside shows.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted a net $411.9 million outflow on Nov. 6, a second straight exit day after Nov. 5's $430.2 million, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show.

Two sessions, about $842 million gone. Bitcoin traded near $75,830 around midnight ET Saturday, up about 0.2% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

BlackRock's IBIT alone accounted for $403.0 million of Friday's redemptions. Fidelity's FBTC took in $42.8 million. Grayscale's GBTC shed $11.1 million, and Bitwise's BITB and Ark 21Shares' ARKB each lost about $20 million.

**How the wrappers move**

A spot bitcoin ETF holds bitcoin and issues shares that trade on U.S. exchanges. When more shares are redeemed than created, the fund sells bitcoin into the market; when creations outrun redemptions, it buys. Friday's net figure is the sum of those share flows across the 12 listed funds Farside tracks, reported in millions of dollars.

U.S. spot ether ETFs also finished Nov. 6 in the red, with a $93.3 million net outflow, Farside's [ether flow page](https://farside.co.uk/eth/) shows. BlackRock's ETHA led that exit at $90.8 million. Solana ETFs posted a $24.2 million net outflow the same day, per Farside's [Solana flow page](https://farside.co.uk/sol/).

The two-day bitcoin-ETF exit follows a $74.6 million inflow on Nov. 4. Crypto Fear & Greed sat at 25, labeled Extreme Fear, on the [CNN Fear & Greed](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/) style index that Alternative.me publishes from market data.

*In our opinion: BlackRock's IBIT did almost all the selling while Fidelity's FBTC took some shares back. The two-day bill is roughly $842 million, and Tuesday's CPI print is the next hard check on whether that pace slows.*

articles.title: Warren Favored to Chair Senate Banking After Midterm Flip
articles.excerpt: The post is not yet formal. She would gain subpoena power over banks, lenders and crypto firms after Democrats flipped both chambers.
articles.body_md:
Sen. Elizabeth Warren is the favorite to become chair of the Senate Banking Committee when Democrats take control of Congress in January, a move that would hand the Massachusetts Democrat subpoena power and a larger staff over banks, lenders, private equity and crypto firms, [Reuters](https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Wall+Street+critic+Elizabeth+Warren+could+be+at+the+height+of+her+power+in+new+Congress/27303260.html) reported Friday.

The assignment is not yet formal. Senate Democrats still have to lock in committee roles. [HousingWire](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/warren-senate-banking-chair/) also reported the expectation Friday, noting that two or three senators could in theory rank ahead of Warren for the chairmanship but are expected to take other posts. She would replace Sen. Tim Scott (R-S.C.) as chair after Democrats flipped both chambers in this week's midterms.

**What a Banking chair can do**

The Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs writes and advances financial legislation and oversees regulators including the Federal Reserve, the OCC, the SEC and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. A chair can schedule hearings, issue subpoenas, demand testimony and set the committee's investigative calendar. Warren is now the top Democrat on the panel as ranking member.

Reuters, citing people familiar with her thinking, said Warren will likely probe the OCC's August decision to approve a bank charter for World Liberty Financial, a crypto project tied to President Donald Trump. The same account said she will examine administration firings of financial-agency staff and efforts to shrink the CFPB, which she helped create. Spokespeople for the OCC and World Liberty did not immediately respond to Reuters. A CFPB spokesperson said the administration is "fixing" what it calls overregulation. A White House spokesperson said Trump is willing to work with anyone on behalf of Americans but that "sham investigations and radical left policies" would undermine that effort.

Warren wrote in a Thursday Time opinion piece that Senate Democrats should probe corporate business dealings and that "Big Tech CEOs, Wall Street executives, and giant corporations should prepare to answer tough questions." She has long criticized crypto firms alongside traditional lenders. Democrats take control of both chambers in January 2027.

Committee assignments are still pending. World Liberty and the OCC had not commented to Reuters by publication on the charter probe her aides flagged.

articles.title: Fed's Daly Sees Further Rate Hikes After Jobs Beat
articles.excerpt: October hiring hit 165,000. Bitcoin was near $75,900 at 5:56 p.m. ET Friday, per CoinGecko, after Thursday's $430.2M ETF outflow.
articles.body_md:
San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said Friday she expects the Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates further to bring inflation down, after a jobs report that showed 165,000 hires in October.

"My expectation is we're going to have to tighten policy further. Exactly when and how much is still to be decided," Daly told [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/fed-daly-interest-rates-inflation.html). "More is likely to be needed." Bloomberg Law also carried her remarks Friday.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics said the unemployment rate edged to 4.1%. That hiring figure was nearly triple the Dow Jones consensus cited by CNBC. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% year over year in October, while September consumer price inflation stood at 3.7%.

**How Fed speak feeds crypto**

When Fed officials lean toward higher policy rates, markets often price firmer Treasury yields and a stronger dollar. Higher yields raise the return on cash and bonds, which can compete with non-yielding assets such as bitcoin for portfolio space. Bitcoin was near $75,900 at about 5:56 p.m. ET Friday, up roughly 0.3% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). That is a flat reading after a week that already saw U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed $430.2 million on Thursday, [Farside Investors](https://www.farside.co.uk/btc/) data shows.

The Federal Open Market Committee raised its overnight target range by a quarter point to 3.75%–4% in September, then held last week to wait for more information. Daly, who votes on the committee next year, said she backed both the September hike and the recent hold. Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin said Thursday he also sees higher rates ahead but is unsure of the timeline, CNBC reported.

Daly called the jobs report "good news for American workers" while saying households remain on a "treadmill of high inflation" after almost six years of elevated prices. She said real wages are falling because pay is not keeping up with inflation.

Bitcoin held near $75,900 into Friday evening ET, per CoinGecko, with Thursday's $430.2 million ETF outflow still the largest flow print of the week on Farside's table.

articles.title: Aave Labs Buys Avon Team to Build Fixed-Rate Lending
articles.excerpt: Terms were not disclosed. Fixed-rate markets are planned work, not a live Aave product in Friday's post, which cites over $33B in deposits.
articles.body_md:
Aave Labs said Friday it has acquired the team and technology behind Avon, a startup that built fixed-rate and floating-rate lending markets and an onchain order book, as the network works to add fixed-rate loans to a platform it says holds more than $33 billion in deposits.

The [Aave Labs blog post](https://aave.com/blog/avon-acquisition) does not disclose financial terms. Prince Sinha and Ayush Kaul are joining the Labs engineering team, and Omar el-Ashaal is joining business development. Avon's fixed- and floating-rate protocols, order book, domains and related assets move with the team. [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/blockchain/2026/aave-labs-acquires-avon-tech-to-take-on-chain-lending-mainstream/) reported the same deal from a Friday release.

**How fixed-rate lending differs onchain**

Most large DeFi lending pools, including Aave's core markets, set borrow rates that float with supply and demand. A fixed-rate loan locks the interest cost for a set term, the way many bank mortgages and corporate credit lines work. Avon's order book was built to match lenders and borrowers for those structures while isolating risk by strategy. Fixed-rate markets on Aave are planned work. Friday's post does not describe a live fixed-rate product.

Aave Labs describes Aave as the largest onchain lending network, with more than $33 billion in deposits and more than $13 billion in active loans in the blog post (an about section on the same page cites more than $30 billion in net deposits). The network is governed by the Aave DAO; Friday's buyer is the Labs contributor entity. The post does not describe a DAO treasury purchase.

"Aave's goal is to bring the best of finance to everyone, and that means offering the kinds of products users already rely on, including fixed rates," founder and CEO Stani Kulechov said in the post. Sinha said the team wants to keep building credit-market depth where it can reach institutions, fintechs and everyday users at scale.

*In our opinion: Aave is buying the team that was already wiring bank-style fixed rates into DeFi, and the price tag stays off the page. That is one way to skip a multi-year build. What to watch next is a public timeline, a test deployment of the order book, or an Aave DAO vote on parameters once Labs is ready to ship.*

articles.title: GOPAX Halts Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat
articles.excerpt: Withdrawals stopped at 2:55 p.m. local time and trading at 3:53 p.m. Assets are moving to cold wallets; no loss has been reported.
articles.body_md:
South Korean crypto exchange GOPAX suspended withdrawals at 2:55 p.m. local time Friday and halted trading at about 3:53 p.m. after receiving an email that claimed the platform had been hacked, the exchange said.

No asset loss has been reported. GOPAX said it had not verified whether the threat was genuine and was moving assets from hot wallets into offline cold storage as a precaution, [Yonhap News Agency](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261106011751320) reported. The [Korea Herald](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10928990) carried the same account.

**What a hot-to-cold shift does**

A hot wallet stays online so the exchange can process customer sends quickly. A cold wallet is kept offline, cut off from the internet, which shrinks the surface an attacker can reach if they have access to online systems. GOPAX said it is transferring remaining hot-wallet balances into cold storage first, then checking security. Standard withdrawals through the website and app are off. Customers who want coins out must apply through the customer support center, where requests are handled manually after internal checks. All open orders were canceled when trading stopped. Deposits of virtual assets were also paused. The company has not set a date to reopen services.

A GOPAX official told Yonhap the email came from a group claiming to have hacked the exchange. "We are prioritizing the protection of customers' assets, even if this causes inconvenience to users," the official said.

The move lands as South Korea's financial sector digests a wider cybersecurity wave. The Financial Services Commission earlier confirmed incidents at 37 financial institutions that affected about 470,000 customer records, Yonhap said. Separately, Korean coverage has noted earlier personal-information leaks at GOPAX this fall; a link between those leaks and Friday's email has not been confirmed.

*In our opinion: customers face stalled access while GOPAX verifies the email and finishes the cold-wallet move. No loss is reported. The next checkable item is the date the exchange restores standard withdrawals and trading; until then, manual support-desk requests are the only path out.*

articles.title: FinCEN Cuts MEXC Off U.S. Finance Over $16B Illicit Claim
articles.excerpt: The order under section 9714 takes effect 30 days after Federal Register publication. MEXC had not issued a public response by late Friday ET.
articles.body_md:
FinCEN on Friday ordered U.S. financial institutions to stop processing funds transfers to or from MEXC Global, saying the offshore crypto exchange facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit transactions from May 2021 through May 2026.

The [Treasury press release](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0685) frames the cut-off as part of Operation Economic Outcast. The order rests on section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. It takes effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. It is a funds-transmittal ban under FinCEN rules. It is separate from an OFAC sanctions listing and does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act or OFAC duties.

**How a 9714 cut-off works**

Section 9714 lets FinCEN bar covered U.S. banks and money transmitters from moving dollars or convertible virtual currency to or from a named foreign exchanger found to be of primary money laundering concern tied to Russian illicit finance. Once the clock starts, those firms face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. MEXC already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its terms, so the practical hit is remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still clear through U.S. institutions.

Treasury says MEXC processed more than $1 billion a day and held about $5 billion in reserves as of September 2026, ranking among the world's 20 largest crypto exchangers. The release alleges nearly $1.5 billion in flows linked to Russian sanctions evasion, including $232 million in direct trades with U.S.-, EU- and UK-sanctioned entities, and continued activity with OFAC-designated Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026. It also cites about $1 billion in direct traffic with more than 40 Iranian crypto exchangers and roughly $22 million tied to Iran's Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Qods Force.

MEXC had not issued a public response to the Friday order by late afternoon ET, [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/fincen-cuts-off-mexc-us-financial-system) reported, noting the exchange's main X account kept posting marketing content through the afternoon. The Federal Register index had not yet posted the notice as of Friday evening, so the 30-day fuse had not started.

*In our opinion: the Register clock is the number that starts the ban. Until that notice posts, covered banks still have a countdown ahead. Watch whether MEXC contests the finding, seeks an exemption, or reroutes liquidity away from U.S. rails once the order bites.*

articles.title: Ex-FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to $2.47 Million Crypto Theft
articles.excerpt: Prosecutors say about 100 transfers used credentials tied to 35 FBI cases. Sentencing is set for March 4, 2027, with a maximum of 20 years.
articles.body_md:
Former FBI agent Patrick Steven Yaroch pleaded guilty on Nov. 5 to wire fraud and money laundering over the theft of about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Virginia said, according to [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/ex-fbi-agents-plea-puts-crypto-theft-at-2-47-million-over-twice-what-he-first-told-the-fbi/) and [FOX 5 DC](https://www.fox5dc.com/news/ex-fbi-agent-pleads-guilty-2-5m-cryptocurrency-theft-scheme-where-he-chatgpt-how-flee-portugal).

Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Va., entered a plea covering roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using wallet credentials linked to 35 FBI investigations, prosecutors said in the plea materials summarized by those outlets. The wallets included accounts tied to subjects of other probes, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI built for an operation, the agreed statement of facts says, as reported.

**How prosecutors describe the scheme**

Yaroch had access to FBI systems that stored crypto credentials collected in investigations. Beginning no later than December 2024, he moved funds out of those wallets, converted them into other tokens and ran further transactions to disguise the trail, according to the plea's statement of facts. Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts and used funds to pay debts such as card balances and car payments, Unchained reported from the Justice Department materials.

The $2.47 million figure is more than double what he first told FBI headquarters in July, when an affidavit recounted his claim of about 10 transfers into a wallet holding roughly $1 million. The [Justice Department Office of the Inspector General](https://oig.justice.gov/news/press-release/fbi-supervisory-special-agent-arrested-following-theft-cryptocurrency) said he was arrested Aug. 4 on a criminal complaint in the Eastern District of Virginia after self-reporting activity in late July. Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea (Case No. 1:26-CR-208). Sentencing is set for March 4, 2027. He faces up to 20 years in prison.

Sentencing is March 4, 2027. The plea locks in the $2.47 million figure and the 35-case credential count that the July self-report understated.

articles.title: DOL Crypto 401(k) Rule Enters Final White House Review
articles.excerpt: RIN 1210-AC38 is a final-rule package from Labor's EBSA, separate from the SEC crypto broker draft reviewed this week. The final text is not public yet.
articles.body_md:
A U.S. Department of Labor final rule on how 401(k) fiduciaries pick investment options, including vehicles that can hold crypto, entered White House review on Nov. 5, an [Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs listing](https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/eoDetails?rrid=1591871) shows.

The package is titled "Fiduciary Duties In Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives" (RIN 1210-AC38). It is staged as a final rule from Labor's Employee Benefits Security Administration, flagged economically significant, and carries no legal deadline. This is a different file from the SEC crypto broker-dealer draft (RIN 3235-AN48) that entered review earlier this week.

**What the March proposal offered**

Labor published the proposal on March 30. Under that draft, plan fiduciaries who follow a documented process when adding alternative assets to a 401(k) menu would receive a process-based safe harbor under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. The six factors named were performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, benchmarks and complexity, [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/dol-rule-crypto-401k-white-house-review) reported, summarizing the DOL proposal and a department fact sheet.

A safe harbor does not require plans to offer crypto. It lowers litigation risk for committees that choose exposure through an allocation sleeve that can hold digital assets, private equity or real estate. The March draft followed President Trump's Aug. 7, 2025, executive order directing Labor to reexamine ERISA guidance on alternative assets in defined-contribution plans. In May 2025 the department had already rescinded a 2022 compliance release that told fiduciaries to use "extreme care" before putting cryptocurrency on a 401(k) menu.

OIRA review under Executive Order 12866 is the last interagency stop before a final rule can be published in the Federal Register. The final wording, any changes to the six-factor test and the effective date will be clear only when Labor posts the cleared text.

*In our opinion: agency and RIN are the map here. Labor's ERISA fiduciary file (1210-AC38) sits apart from the SEC broker rewrite (3235-AN48). The next document to watch is the Federal Register final rule once OIRA returns the Labor package.*

articles.title: Strive Posts $509 Million Q3 Profit on Bitcoin Fair-Value Gains
articles.excerpt: Net unrealized gains on digital assets were $533.7 million in the quarter. The firm bought another 15,124 bitcoin from Oct. 1 through Oct. 30.
articles.body_md:
Strive, Inc. reported GAAP net income of $509.0 million for the three months ended Sept. 30, or $5.24 per diluted common share, driven mainly by bitcoin marked to fair value, the company said in a [GlobeNewswire release](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/06/3397482/0/en/strive-inc-announces-third-quarter-2026-financial-results.html) Friday.

Net unrealized gains on digital assets at fair value were $533.7 million in the quarter. Total revenues were only $2.7 million, mostly investment advisory fees and medical-device sales, so the profit line reflects fair-value marks on the bitcoin book. Operating cash from fees was a thin slice beside it.

**How the bitcoin book moved**

Strive is a Nasdaq-listed firm (ticker ASST) that runs a bitcoin treasury alongside an asset-management unit. Under U.S. crypto accounting rules (ASU 2023-08), bitcoin on the balance sheet is carried at fair value, with gains and losses flowing through net income each period. That means a rising bitcoin price can print a large quarterly profit even when operating revenue is small, and the reverse when prices fall.

The company said it acquired 8,136 bitcoin in the third quarter and 20,373 bitcoin in the nine months through Sept. 30. It bought another 15,124 bitcoin from Oct. 1 through Oct. 30. Digital assets stood at about $2.34 billion fair value on Sept. 30. On Oct. 20 it completed a registered offering of 7 million shares of its 15% Series A Perpetual SATS preferred stock for about $609 million in net proceeds.

Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole said in the release that Strive's year-to-date bitcoin yield is, in his view, the main driver of common equity outperformance versus bitcoin this year. Non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to common stockholders was $494.6 million, or $5.46 per diluted share, after preferred dividends and other adjustments the company defines.

Bitcoin was about $75,920 around noon ET Friday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: the $533.7 million fair-value gain did the heavy lifting beside $2.7 million of revenue. A $509 million profit on a fee book that size is the fair-value rule doing what it says on the tin. Readers watching treasury peers can next check how many bitcoin Strive discloses after October's 15,124-coin add when the next balance sheet lands.*

articles.title: Gnosis Pay Says Hackers Accessed Branded-Card Customer Data
articles.excerpt: The company did not say how many customers were hit. It made 3D Secure mandatory for online card payments until the consumer system retires Dec. 20.
articles.body_md:
Gnosis Pay said Friday that unauthorized access on Nov. 3 exposed certain customer information on the legacy system behind its own branded cards, according to a [company blog post](https://gnosispay.com/blog/data-breach-legacy-system-gnosis-pay-branded-cards).

Containment began within two hours of detection, the firm said. It replaced affected security credentials and fixed the vulnerability. Customer funds were not affected, Gnosis Pay wrote. Its enterprise platform that powers white-label card programs for partners was not hit.

**What changed for card users**

Gnosis Pay is a crypto card provider: users spend stablecoin or crypto balances through a Visa-linked debit card. The breached stack was the B2C branded-card system, already set to retire on Dec. 20, 2026. Until then, the company made 3D Secure, an extra step that confirms online card payments, mandatory for all online charges. It also said it stepped up monitoring of card activity and wallets for fraud.

The firm emailed every affected customer with the specific data taken from their account, reported the incident to partners, the card issuer and data-protection authorities, and said it is arranging specialist monitoring for misuse. It did not publish a headcount of affected customers or a full inventory of data types in the public post.

[Protos](https://protos.com/gnosis-pay-breach-exposes-customer-addresses/) reported that some customer emails described exposure that can include names, shipping or home addresses, card details and linked wallet addresses, citing screenshots shared by users. Gnosis Pay advised customers to treat unexpected messages about their cards as suspect, never share seed phrases, PINs or full card numbers, and be careful sharing home addresses or crypto holdings online or offline.

Gnosis Pay said every affected customer received an email listing exactly what was taken from their account. The consumer branded-card system is still scheduled to retire on Dec. 20.

articles.title: U.S. Adds 165,000 Jobs in October as Unemployment Hits 4.1%
articles.excerpt: August and September payrolls were revised up by a combined 84,000. CME FedWatch odds of a December quarter-point hike rose to about 76.8%.
articles.body_md:
U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October and the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%, the [Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm) reported at 8:30 a.m. ET Friday.

The payroll gain beat the Dow Jones consensus for about 59,000 new jobs cited by [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/jobs-report-october-2026.html). BLS said professional and business services led with 70,000 jobs, health care added 42,000, transportation and warehousing 25,000 and manufacturing 19,000. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month to $38.00, up 3.1% over 12 months.

**How the report feeds the Fed**

The Employment Situation mixes two surveys. The establishment survey counts payroll jobs by industry. The household survey drives the unemployment rate. Stronger hiring and a firmer wage print can keep inflation pressure in view, which is why rate futures often reprice after the release.

August payrolls were revised up by 53,000 to 186,000 and September by 31,000 to 60,000, BLS said, a combined 84,000 more jobs than previously reported. The labor force participation rate stood at 61.9%. People working part time for economic reasons rose by 339,000 to 4.8 million.

After the print, CME Group's FedWatch tool showed about a 76.8% chance of a quarter-point rate increase at the Dec. 8-9 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, CNBC reported, up from levels before the release. A [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/traders-raise-bets-of-fed-rate-hike-after-jobs-report-5008229) dispatch put futures pricing near an 80% probability of a December hike.

Bitcoin was about $75,920 around noon ET Friday (down about 0.6% over 24 hours), per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: for crypto readers, the stake sits at the December FOMC. A higher overnight rate can tighten liquidity for non-yielding assets. The next hard check is the Fed's own statement on Dec. 9.*

articles.title: FinCEN and Fed Withdraw $250 Cross-Border Travel Rule Plan
articles.excerpt: The 2020 proposal also sought to spell out Travel Rule coverage for convertible virtual currency. Publication of the withdrawal is set for Nov. 9.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Federal Reserve Board are withdrawing a 2020 plan that would have cut the threshold for collecting, retaining and transmitting information on cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250, a [Federal Register public-inspection notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/2026-22809/threshold-for-the-requirement-to-collect-retain-and-transmit-information-on-funds-transfers-and) filed Friday shows.

The agencies said they will not take further action on the joint notice of proposed rulemaking published Oct. 27, 2020. The withdrawal is scheduled for Federal Register publication on Nov. 9. The existing $3,000 Recordkeeping Rule and Travel Rule thresholds stay in place.

**What the 2020 plan would have changed**

Under Bank Secrecy Act rules often called the Recordkeeping Rule and the Travel Rule, banks and nonbank financial institutions must collect, keep and pass on sender and recipient details for funds transfers of $3,000 or more. The 2020 proposal would have lowered that bar to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. FinCEN also proposed clarifying that "money" in those rules covers domestic and cross-border transactions in convertible virtual currency and digital assets with legal tender status.

The agencies received nearly 3,000 comments. Most opposed the lower threshold, citing burden on smaller institutions, remittance costs and weak supporting data, the withdrawal notice says. Views on applying the rules expressly to crypto were mixed: crypto service firms often objected on technology and messaging standards, while some banks and money services businesses supported that piece.

FinCEN and the Fed gave two reasons for pulling the file. More than five years have passed, and they want fresh public comment before any similar rewrite. They also pointed to newer crypto frameworks, including the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted in July 2025, and said future Travel Rule changes for crypto should fit those developments.

*In our opinion: $3,000 is still the live Travel Rule line for these transfers. Nov. 9 is when the withdrawal hits the Federal Register; any crypto-specific rewrite would need a fresh comment round after GENIUS-era stablecoin rules.*
